336.sa: तेषां कथयतां तत्र सर्वांस्ताननुमान्य च। ततो वृद्धतमस्तेषां जाम्बवान्प्रत्यभाषत।।4.65.10।।
336.e: When the monkeys were talking (of their individual capacity) in that manner about their speed, Jambavan the oldest of the monkeys inferred (their capacity) and said:

336.sa: पूर्वमस्माकमप्यासीत्कश्चिद्गतिपराक्रमः। ते वयं वयसः पारमनुप्राप्तास्स्म साम्प्रतम्।।4.65.11।।
336.e: 'Earlier I was also very courageous, but now I have become old and reached the fag end of life.

336.sa: किन्तु नैवं गते शक्यमिदं कार्यमुपेक्षितुम्। यदर्थं कपिराजश्च रामश्च कृतनिश्चयौ।।4.65.12।।
336.e: 'However  in this situation, it is not possible for us to neglect (our task) as it is the order of the monkeyking and Rama who are determined to achieve the objective.

336.sa: साम्प्रतं कालभेदेन या गतिस्तां निबोधत। नवतिं योजनानां तु गमिष्यामि न संशयः।।4.65.13।।
तांश्च सर्वान्हरिश्रेष्ठाञ्जाम्बवान्पुनरब्रवीत्। न खल्वेतावदेवासीद्गमने मे पराक्रमः।।4.65.14।।
336.e: Jambavan, the distinguished among the monkeys again said, 'My strength to leap into the sky was not only that much (I was stronger in my youth and could cover longer distances)'

336.sa: मया महाबलेश्चैव यज्ञे विष्णुस्सनातनः। प्रदक्षिणीकृतः पूर्वं क्रममाणस्त्रिविक्रमम्।।4.65.15।।
336.e: 'In the past, at the time of the wellknown yagna (of king Bali) I was very strong. I circumambulated the eternal Vishnu while he was taking three strides (in his incarnation of Trivikrama Vamana.)

336.sa: स इदानीमहं वृद्धः प्लवने मन्दविक्रमः। यौवने च तदाऽसीन्मे बलमप्रतिमं परैः।।4.65.16।।
336.e: 'Having grown old I do not have the same courage. In my youth my prowess was incomparable and none could excel me.

336.sa: सम्प्रत्येतावतीं शक्तिं गमने तर्कयाम्यहम्। नैतावता हि संसिद्धिः कार्यस्यास्य भविष्यति।।4.65.17।।
336.e: 'I guess that at this time I do not have the capacity to fly to that extent. Achieving the objective is out of question with this much of energy.

336.sa: अथोत्तरमुदारार्थमब्रवीदङ्गदस्तदा। अनुमान्य तथा प्राज्ञो जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिम्।।4.65.18।।
336.e: 'Then the wise Angada said to great Jambavan, in a gentle manner about his  own strength.

336.sa: अहमेतद्गमिष्यामि योजनानां शतं महत्। निवर्तने तु मे शक्तिस्स्यान्न वेति न निश्चितम्।।4.65.19।।
336.e: 'I can  certainly go to a distance of a hundred yojanas. However, I cannot say whether I will have enough capacity to return?

336.sa: तमुवाच हरिश्रेष्ठं जाम्बवान्वाक्यकोविदः। ज्ञायते गमने शक्तिस्तव हर्यृक्षसत्तम।।4.65.20।।
336.e: Jambavan who was skilful in speech spoke to that great Angada, 'O leader among monkeys and bears your energy to cover this distance is wellknown to us'.

336.sa: कामं शतं सहस्रं वा न ह्येष विधिरुच्यते। योजनानां भवान् शक्तो गन्तुं प्रतिनिवर्तितुम्।।4.65.21।।
336.e: 'You can go upto even a hundred thousand yojanas and have the required energy to return also. But it is not proper to send you (because you are the heir apparent).

336.sa: न हि प्रेषयिता तात स्वामी प्रेष्यः कथञ्चन। भवताऽयं जनस्सर्वः प्रेष्यः प्लवगसत्तम।।4.65.22।।
भवान्कळत्रमस्माकं स्वामिभावे व्यवस्थितः। स्वामी कळत्रं सैन्यस्य गतिरेषा परन्तप।।4.65.23।।
336.e: 'O scorcher of enemies, you are established as the commander of the army and it is proper for us to protect you as we protect our wives.

336.sa: अपि चैतस्य कार्यस्य भवान्मूलमरिन्दम। तस्मात्कळत्रवत्तात प्रतिपाल्यस्सदा भवान्।।4.65.24।।
336.e: 'O subduer of enemies in acomplishing this task you are the root. O dear therefore you should always be taken care of by us just like the wife looked after.

336.sa: मूलमर्थस्य संरक्ष्यमेष कार्यविदां नयः। मूले सति हि सिद्ध्यन्ति गुणा फलो पुष्पोदयाः।।4.65.25।।
336.e: 'The root of any objective should be protected well. This is the basis of an accomplisher. Only when the roots are intact, the trees have the ability to yield flowers and fruits.

336.sa: तद्भवानस्य कार्यस्य साधने सत्यविक्रम। बुद्धिविक्रमसम्पन्नो हेतुरत्र परन्तप।।4.65.26।।
336.e: 'O warrior of proven valour O subduer of enemies in achieving this objective you are the source, being endowed with valour and wisdom.

336.sa: गुरुश्च गुरुपुत्रश्च त्वं हि नः कपिसत्तम। भवन्तमाश्रित्य वयं समर्था ह्यर्थसाधने।।4.65.27।।
336.e: 'O best of monkeys you are the son of my guide (Vali) and respectable. We will be capable of accomplishing the goal only under your protection and guidance.

336.sa: उक्तवाक्यं महाप्राज्ञं जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिः। प्रत्युवाचोत्तरं वाक्यं वालिसूनुरथाङ्गदः।।4.65.28।।
336.e: Jambavan, the wise monkey having said that, Angada, the great son of Vali, replied:

336.sa: यदि नाहं गमिष्यामि नान्यो वानरपुङ्गवः। पुनः खल्विदमस्माभिः कार्यं प्रायोपवेशनम्।।4.65.29।।
336.e: 'If I do not go and no other monkey leader goes, then we have to resort to fasting unto death once again.

336.sa: न ह्यकृत्वा हरिपतेस्सन्देशं तस्य धीमतः। तत्रापि गत्वा प्राणानां पश्यामि परिरक्षणम्।।4.65.30।।
336.e: 'If I do not fulfil the objective of the wise king of monkeys I cannot save my life even after returning there (Kishkinda).

336.sa: स हि प्रसादे चात्यर्थं कोपे च हरिरीश्वरः। अतीत्य तस्य सन्देशं विनाशो गमने भवेत्।।4.65.31।।
336.e: 'The monkey king has the authority to shower grace or give vent to his anger. If we go without fulfilling the task we will face destruction.

336.sa: तद्यथा ह्यस्य कार्यस्य न भवत्यन्यथा गतिः। तद्भवानेव दृष्टार्थस्सञ्चिन्तयितु मर्हति।।4.65.32।।
336.e: 'Therefore, think over well so that we do not fail ultimately. You have a vision.You should suggest means by which this mission does not misfire.'

336.sa: सोऽङ्गदेन तदा वीरः प्रत्युक्तः प्लवगर्षभः। जाम्बवानुत्तरं वाक्यं प्रोवाचेदं ततोऽङ्गदम्।।4.65.33।।
336.e: On listening to Angada's words, Jambavan, the  bull among monkeys, replied this way:

336.sa: अस्य ते वीर कार्यस्य न किञ्चित्परिहीयते। एष सञ्चोदयाम्येनं यः कार्यं साधयिष्यति।।4.65.34।।
336.e: 'O hero this work will not be balked. I will now inspire one who can achieve this task.'

337.sa: अनेकशतसाहस्रीं विषण्णां हरिवाहिनीम्। जाम्बवान्समुदीक्ष्यैवं हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्।।4.66.1।।
337.e: Then Jambavan observed the worries of several hundred thousands of the monkey army and said to Hanuman:

337.sa: वीर वानरलोकस्य सर्वशास्त्रविदां वर। तूष्णीमेकान्तमाश्रित्य हनूमन्किं न जल्पसि।।4.66.2।।
337.e: 'O Hanuman you are the choicest one among many scholars wellversed in all sastras. Why do you sit alone? Why do you not speak?

337.sa: हनूमन्हरिराजस्य सुग्रीवस्य समो ह्यसि। रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि तेजसा च बलेन च।।4.66.3।।
337.e: 'Hanuman you are equal to the king of monkeys and also Rama and Lakshmana in brilliance and strength.

337.sa: अरिष्टनेमिनः पुत्रो वैनतेयो महाबलः। गरुत्मानिति विख्यात उत्तमस्सर्वपक्षिणाम्।।4.66.4।।
337.e: 'You are the son of Arishtanemi (sage Kasyapa) and Vinata, and your gurulike (elder brother) is Garuda, the greatest among birds. He is powerful and and famous.

337.sa: बहुशो हि मया दृष्टः सागरे स महाबलः। भुजङ्गानुद्धरन्पक्षी महावेगो महायशाः।।4.66.5।।
337.e: 'Garuda is very powerful, swift, and famous. I have seen him snatching serpents from the ocean many times.

337.sa: पक्षयोर्यद्बलं तस्य तावद्भुजबलं तव। विक्रमश्चापि वेगश्च न ते तेनावहीयते।।4.66.6।।
337.e: 'The strength of your shoulders is equal to that of his (Garuda's) wings. Your speed and valour are no less.

337.sa: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न बुध्यसे।।4.66.7।।
337.e: 'O leader of the monkeys you are superior in strength, wisdom, brilliance and valour to all beings. Why do you not realise your own strength?

337.sa: अप्सराप्सरसां श्रेष्ठा विख्याता पुञ्जिकस्थला। अञ्जनेति परिख्याता पत्नी केसरिणो हरेः।।4.66.8।।
विख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि। अभिशापादभूत्तात वानरी कामरूपिणी।।4.66.9।।
337.e: 'O dear she was famous in the three worlds, peerless in beauty and could change form at her free will. She was born of a monkey on this land by dint of a curse.

337.sa: दुहिता वानरेन्द्रस्य कुञ्जरस्य महात्मनः। मानुषं विग्रहं कृत्वा रूपयौवनशालिनी।।4.66.10।। विचित्रमाल्याभरणा महार्हक्षौमवासिनी। अचरत्पर्वतस्याग्रे प्रावृडम्बुदसन्निभे।।4.66.11।।
337.e: 'She was the daughter of a great king of monkeys called Kunjara. That young and beautiful lady had assumed a lustrous human form decked with wonderful garlands, ornaments and silk clothes and was roving on top of the mountain which appeared like a proud raincloud.

337.sa: दुहिता वानरेन्द्रस्य कुञ्जरस्य महात्मनः। मानुषं विग्रहं कृत्वा रूपयौवनशालिनी।।4.66.10।। विचित्रमाल्याभरणा महार्हक्षौमवासिनी। अचरत्पर्वतस्याग्रे प्रावृडम्बुदसन्निभे।।4.66.11।।
337.e: 'She was the daughter of a great king of monkeys called Kunjara. That young and beautiful lady had assumed a lustrous human form decked with wonderful garlands, ornaments and silk clothes and was roving on top of the mountain which appeared like a proud raincloud.

337.sa: तस्या वस्त्रं विशालाक्ष्याः पीतं रक्तदशं शुभम्। स्थितायाः पर्वतस्याग्रे मारुतोऽपहरच्छनैः।।4.66.12।।
337.e: 'While the largeeyed lady was stationed on the mountain top, the Windgod gently let her auspicious yellow garment with red border fly away.

337.sa: स ददर्श ततस्तस्या वृत्तावूरू सुसंहतौ। स्तनौ च पीनौ सहितौ सुजातं चारु चाननम्।।4.66.13।।
337.e: 'Then he (Windgod) saw her curved, wellset thighs, her beautiful plump breasts and her lovely pleasing face.

337.sa: तां विशालायतश्रोणीं तनुमध्यां यशस्विनीम्। दृष्टवैव शुभसर्वाङ्गीं पवनः काममोहितः।।4.66.14।।
337.e: 'On seeing the broad hips, slender waist and beautiful limbs of that famous lady the Windgod was infatuated.

337.sa: स तां भुजाभ्यां दीर्घाभ्यां पर्यष्वजत मारुतः। मन्मथाविष्टसर्वाङ्गो गतात्मा तामनिन्दिताम्।।4.66.15।।
337.e: 'The Windgod lost his control over himself. His whole being was overpowered by love for her beautiful, flawless body. He embraced her with his long arms.

337.sa: सा तु तत्रैव सम्भ्रान्ता सुव्रता वाक्यमब्रवीत्। एकपत्नीव्रतमिदं को नाशयितुमिच्छति।।4.66.16।।
337.e: 'She was bewildered by this and being chaste and strict observer of chastiny she said, 'Who is it that has destroyed my monoandry?

337.sa: अञ्जनाया वच्शुत्वा मारुतः प्रत्यभाषत। न त्वां हिंसामि सुश्रोणि मा भूत्ते सुभगे भयम्।।4.66.17।।
337.e: 'On hearing Anjana's words, the Windgod replied, ' O auspicious lady, I do you no harm, O lady of beautiful hips. I reached (enjoyed) you in mind, not body. You need not fear.'

337.sa: मनसाऽस्मि गतो यत्त्वां परिष्वज्य यशस्विनीम्। वीर्यवान्बुद्धिसम्पन्न: पुत्रस्तव भविष्यति।।4.66.18।।
337.e: 'O renowned lady I have embraced you and united with you mentally (enjoyed you without physical contact).You will bring forth a son endowed with great wisdom and courage.

337.sa: महासत्त्वो महातेजा महाबलपराक्रमः। लङ्घने प्लवने चैव भविष्यति हि मत्समः।।4.66.19।।
337.e: 'He will be very powerful, illustrious and will be of great valour and strength. He will be my equal in leaping and flying'.

337.sa: एवमुक्ता ततस्तुष्टा जननी ते महाकपे। गुहायां त्वां महाबाहो प्रजज्ञे प्लवगर्षभम्।।4.66.20।।
337.e: 'O great monkey O strongshouldered one having been assured that way, your mother was pleased and delivered you, a bull among monkeys, in a cave.

337.sa: अभ्युत्थितं ततस्सूर्यं बालो दृष्ट्वा महावने। फलं चेति जिघृक्षुस्त्वमुत्प्लुत्याभ्युद्गतो दिवम्।।4.66.21।।
337.e: 'On seeing the rising Sun in the deep forest, mistaking him to be a fruit, you wanted to seize it, when you were young.You suddenly flew into the sky and went flying towards the Sun.

337.sa: शतानि त्रीणि गत्वाऽथ योजनानां महाकपे। तेजसा तस्य निर्धूतो न विषादं ततोगतः।।4.66.22।।
337.e: 'O great monkey you went three hundred yojanas and were pushed back by the  Sun's radiance. Yet it did not leave you depressed.

337.sa: तावदापपत स्तूर्णमन्तरिक्षं महाकपे। क्षिप्तमिन्द्रेण ते वज्रं कोपाविष्टेन धीमता।।4.66.23।।
337.e: 'O great monkey while falling fast in space, wise Indra hurled his thunderbolt quickly at you, in anger.

337.sa: तदा शैलाग्रशिखरे वामो हनुरभज्यत। ततो हि नामधेयं ते हनुमानिति कीर्त्यते।।4.66.24।।
337.e: 'You fell on the edge of the mountain peak and your left chin  got broken. Since then you are widely known as Hanuman (one who has a wounded chin).

337.sa: तस्त्वावि निहतं दृष्ट्वा वायुर्गन्धवहस्स्वयम्। त्रैलोक्ये भृशसङ्कृद्धो न ववौ वै प्रभञ्जनः।।4.66.25।।
337.e: The Windgod who is a carrier of fragrance and breaker of trees became very angry on seeing (the injury on) you and stopped blowing in the three worlds.

337.sa: सम्भ्रान्ताश्च सूरास्सर्वे त्रैलोक्ये क्षुभिते सति। प्रसादयन्ति संक्रुद्धं मारुतं भुवनेश्वराः।।4.66.26।।
प्रसादिते च पवने ब्रह्मा तुभ्यं वरं ददौ। अशस्त्रवध्यतां तात समरे सत्यविक्रम।।4.66.27।।
337.e: 'O dear when the Windgod was pleased, Brahma gave a boon to you, to appease his anger. The boon made you truly valiant so that you cannot be struck by any weapon and killed.

337.sa: वज्रस्य च निपातेन विरुजं त्वां समीक्ष्य च। सहस्रनेत्रः प्रीतात्मा ददौ ते वरमुत्तमम्।।4.66.28।। स्वच्छन्दतश्च मरणं तेभूयादिति वै प्रभो।
337.e: 'O lord observing that you are not hurt even when struck by the thunderbolt, Indra offered, one of the best boons to you, to choose to die only when you wish.

337.sa: स त्वं केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीमविक्रमः।।4.66.29।। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तेजसा चापि तत्समः। त्वं हि वायुसुतो वत्स प्लवने चापि तत्समः।।4.66.30।।
337.e: 'You are a son of Kesari endowed with terrific strength and a lawful son of Maruta also. You are, therefore, equal to the very Windgod in flying and in brilliance.

337.sa: स त्वं केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीमविक्रमः।।4.66.29।। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तेजसा चापि तत्समः। त्वं हि वायुसुतो वत्स प्लवने चापि तत्समः।।4.66.30।।
337.e: 'You are a son of Kesari endowed with terrific strength and a lawful son of Maruta also. You are, therefore, equal to the very Windgod in flying and in brilliance.

337.sa: वयमद्य गतप्राणा भवान्नस्त्रातु साम्प्रतम्। दाक्ष्यविक्रमसम्पन्नः कपिराज इवापरः।।4.66.31।।
337.e: 'Now we have almost lost our life.You are our saviour like another monkeyking (like Garuda, king of birds).You are fully endowed with valour and courage.

337.sa: त्रिविक्रमे मया तात सशैलवनकानना। त्रिस्सप्तकृत्वः पृथिवी परिक्रान्ता प्रदक्षिणम्।।4.66.32।।
337.e: 'O dear when Visnu (Vamana incarnate) took three strides I circumambulated the whole earth including its mountains and trees twentyone times.

337.sa: तथा चौषधयोऽस्माभिस्सञ्चिता देवशासनात्। निष्पन्नममृतं याभिस्तदासीन्नो महद्बलम्।।4.66.33।।
337.e: 'Then on receiving orders from the gods, we collected medicinal herbs and nectar which gave us great strength.

337.sa: स इदानीमहं वृद्धः परिहीनपराक्रमः। साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं भवान्सर्वगुणान्वितः।।4.66.34।।
337.e: 'I have become old and my valour is depleted. At this time you are the sole resort for us. You have all the necessary qualities.

337.sa: तद्विजृम्भस्व विक्रान्त: प्लवतामुत्तमो ह्यसि। त्वद्वीर्यं द्रष्टुकामा हि सर्वा वानरवाहिनी।।4.66.35।।
337.e: 'Cheer up and advance.You are the best among the creatures that can leap.The entire army of monkeys want to see your valour.

337.sa: उत्तिष्ठ हरिशार्दूल लङ्घयस्व महार्णवम्। परा हि सर्वभूतानां हनुमन्या गतिस्तव।।4.66.36।।
337.e: 'O Hanuman, tiger among monkeys, rise up and cross this great ocean.You have that supreme capacity among all beings.

337.sa: विषण्णा हरयस्सर्वे हनुमन्किमुपेक्षसे। विक्रमस्व महावेगो विष्णुस्त्रीन्विक्रमानिव।।4.66.37।।
337.e: 'O Hanuman All the monkeys look dejected. Why do you delay? O warrior, act quick with your rapid speed like Trivikrama who took three strides that covered the entire universe'.

338.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा जृम्भमाणं ते क्रमितुं शतयोजनम्। वीर्येणापूर्यमाणं च सहसा वानरोत्तमम्।।4.67.1।। सहसा शोकमुत्सृज्य प्रहर्षेण समन्विताः। विनेदुस्तुष्टुवुश्चापि हनूमन्तं महाबलम्।।4.67.2।।
338.e: 'In order to cross a hundred yojanas, Hanuman, the best of monkeys expanded his  might and strength. Seeing him, a warrior of great strength, all the monkeys, filled with enthusiasm at once gave up grief and collected together.They rejoiced and propitiated him screaming aloud.

338.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा जृम्भमाणं ते क्रमितुं शतयोजनम्। वीर्येणापूर्यमाणं च सहसा वानरोत्तमम्।।4.67.1।। सहसा शोकमुत्सृज्य प्रहर्षेण समन्विताः। विनेदुस्तुष्टुवुश्चापि हनूमन्तं महाबलम्।।4.67.2।।
338.e: 'In order to cross a hundred yojanas, Hanuman, the best of monkeys expanded his  might and strength. Seeing him, a warrior of great strength, all the monkeys, filled with enthusiasm at once gave up grief and collected together.They rejoiced and propitiated him screaming aloud.

338.sa: प्रहृष्टा विस्मिताश्चैव वीक्षन्ते स्म समन्ततः। त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहं नारायणमिव प्रजाः।।4.67.3।।
338.e: The monkeys collected together happily, gazing at Hanuman.They were wonderstruck to see Hanuman in that huge form, just as all beings were when they saw Lord Narayana in his incarnation of Vamana.

338.sa: संस्तूयमानो हनुमान्व्यवर्धत महाबलः। समाविध्य च लाङ्गूलं हर्षाद्बलमुपेयिवान्।।4.67.4।।
338.e: The monkeys praised the mighty Hanuman as he grew in size whirling his tail around joyfully.

338.sa: तस्य संस्तूयमानस्य सर्वैर्वानरपुङ्गवैः। तेजसापूर्यमाणस्य रूपमासीदनुत्तमम्।।4.67.5।।
338.e: As Hanuman was being praised by the monkey leaders, his body filled with lustre. It looked excellent.

338.sa: यथा विजृम्भते सिंहो विवृद्धो गिरिगह्वरे। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तथा सम्प्रति जृम्भते।।4.67.6।।
338.e: Just as a lion grown in a mountain cave stretches its body, the Windgod's son stretched  (his limbs) at that time.

338.sa: अशोभत मुखं तस्य जृम्भमाणस्य धीमतः। अम्बरीषमिवाऽदीप्तं विधूम इव पावकः।।4.67.7।।
338.e: On expansion, wise Hanuman's face was bright, glowing like a burning oven and  shining like smokeless fire.

338.sa: हरीणामुत्थितो मध्यात्सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः। अभिवाद्य हरीन्वृद्धान्हनुमानिदमब्रवीत्।।4.67.8।।
338.e: Hanuman risen from the midst of the monkeys with his hair bristling on the body (due to expansion of body), saluted reverentially to the elderly monkey Jambavan and said :

338.sa: अरुजत्सर्वताग्राणि हुताशनसखोऽनिलः। बलवानप्रमेयश्च वायुराकाशगोचरः।।4.67.9।।
338.e: 'The Windgod is a friend of fire who is a powerful consumer of oblations. His strength is immeasurable. He wanders in the sky and shatters the mountain tops.

338.sa: तस्याहं शीघ्रवेगस्य शीघ्रगस्य महात्मनः। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रः प्लवनेनास्मि तत्समः।।4.67.10।।
338.e: 'I am the lawfulson of the swiftmoving Windgod, Maruta, comparable to him in leaping.

338.sa: उत्सहेयं हि विस्तीर्णमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्। मेरुं गिरिमसङ्गेन परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः।।4.67.11।।
338.e: 'I can with all enthusiasm go round the vast mount Meru a thousand times without resting on it which is as though scratching the sky.

338.sa: बाहुवेगप्रणुन्नेन सागरेणाहमुत्सहे। समाप्लावयितुं लोकं सपर्वतनदीह्रदम्।।4.67.12।।
338.e: 'I can submerge this world including its mountains rivers and lakes. I can push back the sea waters quickly with my arms.

338.sa: ममोरुजङ्घावेगेन भविष्यति समुत्थितः। सम्मूर्च्छितमहाग्राहस्समुद्रो वरुणालयः।।4.67.13।।
338.e: 'Thrust by my thighs,the ocean will rise up, carrying with it the shanks and  mighty crocodiles stunned by the force.

338.sa: पन्नगाशनमाकाशे पतन्तं पक्षिसेविते। वैनतेयमहं शक्तः परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः।।4.67.14।।
338.e: 'I am capable of circumambulating a thousand times the great Garuda who consumes snakes and flies in the sky, the abode of birds.

338.sa: उदयात्प्रस्थितं वापि ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्। अनस्तमितमादित्यमभिगन्तुं समुत्सहे।।4.67.15।। ततो भूमिमसंस्पृश्य पुनरागन्तुमुत्सहे। प्रवेगेनैव महता भीमेन प्लवगर्षभाः।।4.67.16।।
338.e: 'O bull among monkeys when the Sun rises from behind the eastern mountain it is possible for me to start with him and go to the western horizon and return before the blazing Sun with its beams of light sets. It is also possible for me to descend to  the earth with the same speed and return to the Sun without touching the earth.

338.sa: उदयात्प्रस्थितं वापि ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्। अनस्तमितमादित्यमभिगन्तुं समुत्सहे।।4.67.15।। ततो भूमिमसंस्पृश्य पुनरागन्तुमुत्सहे। प्रवेगेनैव महता भीमेन प्लवगर्षभाः।।4.67.16।।
338.e: 'O bull among monkeys when the Sun rises from behind the eastern mountain it is possible for me to start with him and go to the western horizon and return before the blazing Sun with its beams of light sets. It is also possible for me to descend to  the earth with the same speed and return to the Sun without touching the earth.

338.sa: उत्सहेयमतिक्रान्तुं सर्वानाकाशगोचरान्। सागरं क्षोभयिष्यामि दारयिष्यामि मेदिनीम्।।4.67.17।।
338.e: 'If I rise up, I can overtake all those creatures flying in the sky and from there I can stir up the ocean and tear up the earth easily.

338.sa: पर्वतांश्चूर्णयिष्यामि प्लवमानः प्लवङ्गमाः। हरिष्याम्यूरुवेगेन प्लवमानो महार्णवम्।।4.67.18।।
338.e: 'O monkeys when I leap, I can crush the mountains into powder and pull the vast ocean with me with the force of my thighs.

338.sa: लतानां विविधं पुष्पं पादपानां च सर्वशः। अनुयास्यन्ति मामद्य प्लवमानं विहायसा।।4.67.19।।
338.e: And then as I leap through the sky flowers of many kinds of creepers and trees will follow me.

338.sa: भविष्यति हि मे पन्थास्स्वातेः पन्था इवाम्बरे। चरन्तं घोरमाकाशमुत्पतिष्यन्तमेव वा।।4.67.20।। द्रक्ष्यन्ति निपतिष्यन्तं च सर्वभूतानि वानराः।
338.e: 'O monkey when I fly upward in the dreadful sky or descend down, all creatures will see me, for my path will be the path of the constellation of Swati (a group of stars).

338.sa: महामेरुप्रतीकाशं मां द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः।।4.67.21।। दिवमावृत्य गच्छन्तं ग्रसमानमिवाम्बरम्।
338.e: 'O monkeys when I fly in the sky like the great mount Meru, you will see me as if I am swallowing the sky because I will be enveloping it with my strides.

338.sa: विधमिष्यामि जीमूतान्कम्पयिष्यामि पर्वतान्।।4.67.22।। सागरं शोषयिष्यामि प्लवमानस्समाहितः।
वैनतेयस्य या शक्तिर्मम सा मारुतस्य वा।।4.67.23।। ऋते सुपर्णराजानं मारुतं वा महाजवम्। न तद्भूतं प्रपश्यामि यन्मां प्लुतमनुव्रजेत्।।4.67.24।।
338.e: 'Only Garuda and Maruta have the capacity to fly like me. No one other than the king of vultures and the Windgod have the speed to fly like me.

338.sa: वैनतेयस्य या शक्तिर्मम सा मारुतस्य वा।।4.67.23।। ऋते सुपर्णराजानं मारुतं वा महाजवम्। न तद्भूतं प्रपश्यामि यन्मां प्लुतमनुव्रजेत्।।4.67.24।।
338.e: 'Only Garuda and Maruta have the capacity to fly like me. No one other than the king of vultures and the Windgod have the speed to fly like me.

338.sa: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण निरालम्बनमम्बरम्। सहसा निपतिष्यामि घनाद्विद्युदिवोत्थिता।।4.67.25।।
338.e: 'Just as the lightning generated by the clouds lands at once flying in the sky without any support I can also land in less than a moment.

338.sa: भविष्यति हि मे रूपं प्लवमानस्य सागरे। विष्णोर्विक्रममाणस्य पुरा त्रीन्विक्रमानिव।।4.67.26।।
बुद्ध्या चाहं प्रपश्यामि मनश्चेष्टा च मे तथा। अहं द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेहीं प्रमोदध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.67.27।।
338.e: 'O monkeys I have a feeling in my mind that I will see Vaidehi. Be happy.

338.sa: मारुतस्य समो वेगे गरुडस्य समो जवे। अयुतं योजनानां तु गमिष्यामीति मे मतिः।।4.67.28।।
338.e: 'I am equal to Maruta and Garuda in speed. I feel I can cover ten thousand yojanas (at a stretch).

338.sa: वासवस्य सवज्रस्य ब्रह्मणो वा स्वयम्भुवः। विक्रम्य सहसा हस्तादमृतं तदिहानये।।4.67.29।। लङ्कां वापि समुत्क्षिप्य गच्छेयमिति मे मतिः।
338.e: 'I think I can encounter Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt and obtain nectar from his hands. I can even confront Brahma, the selfborn creator courageously. I can even uproot Lanka and carry it.'

338.sa: तमेवं वानरश्रेष्ठं गर्जन्तममितौजसम्।।4.67.30।। प्रहृष्टा हरयस्तत्र समुदैक्षन्त विस्मिताः।
338.e: The monkeys looked at him and were amazed, happy to see him roaring and shining in brilliance.

338.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ज्ञातीनां शोकनाशनम्।।4.67.31।। उवाच परिसंहृष्टो जाम्बवान्हरिसत्तमः।
338.e: Jambavan, the finest of the monkeys, felt very glad on hearing his words which put an end to the sorrow of the kith and kin and said:

338.sa: वीर केसरिणः पुत्र हनुमान्मारुतात्मज।।4.67.32।। ज्ञातीनां विपुलश्शोकस्त्वया तात प्रणाशितः।
338.e: 'O son of Kesari O son of Maruta O hero you have removed the great grief of your race, dear

338.sa: तव कल्याणरुचयः कपिमुख्यास्समागताः।।4.67.33।। मङ्गलं कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं करिष्यन्ति समाहिताः।
ऋषीणां च प्रसादेन कपिवृद्धमतेन च।।4.67.34।। गुरूणां च प्रसादेन प्लवस्व त्वं महार्णवम्।
338.e: 'By the blessings of the sages and by the grace of the elderly monkeys may you cross over the vast ocean.

338.sa: स्थास्यामश्चैकपादेन यावदागमनं तव।।4.67.35।। त्वद्गतानि च सर्वेषां जीवनानि वनौकसाम्।
ततस्तु हरिशार्दूलस्तानुवाच वनौकसः।।4.67.36।। नेयं मम मही वेगं लङ्घने धारयिष्यति।
338.e: Then the tiger among monkeys, Hanuman said to those forestdwellers (monkeys), 'The earth cannot bear the thrust of my leaping.

338.sa: एतानीह नगस्यास्य शिलासङ्कटशालिनः।।4.67.37।। शिखराणि महेन्द्रस्य स्थिराणि सुमहान्ति च।
338.e: 'The rocks on the peaks of the ranges of mount Mahendra cannot with stand it, although they are huge and firm.

338.sa: एषु वेगं करिष्यामि महेन्द्रशिखरेष्वहम्।।4.67.38।। नानाद्रुमविकीर्णेषु धातुनिष्यन्दशोभिषु।
338.e: 'I will pick up speed on the peaks of mount Mahendra filled with different kinds of trees and minerals.

338.sa: एतानि मम निष्पेषं पादयोः प्लवतां वराः।।4.67.39।। प्लवतो धारयिष्यन्ति योजनानामितश्शतम्।
338.e: 'O great monkeys these mountain peaks can withstand the crushing force of my feet as I leap over a hundred yojanas.

338.sa: ततस्तं मारुतप्रख्यस्सहरिर्मारुतात्मजः।।4.67.40।। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः। वृतं नानाविधैः वृक्षैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्।।4.67.41।। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्। सिंहशार्दूलचरितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्।।4.67.42।। मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम्।
338.e: The son of Maruta, who was as eminent as the Windgod, the crusher of enemies ascended the great mountain Mahendra, full of grassland inhabited by deer, thickly grown with various trees and creepers full of fragrant flowers and fruits, where roam lions and tigers and proud elephants, a place that echoes with sounds of intoxicated birds and waterfalls.

338.sa: ततस्तं मारुतप्रख्यस्सहरिर्मारुतात्मजः।।4.67.40।। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः। वृतं नानाविधैः वृक्षैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्।।4.67.41।। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्। सिंहशार्दूलचरितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्।।4.67.42।। मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम्।
338.e: The son of Maruta, who was as eminent as the Windgod, the crusher of enemies ascended the great mountain Mahendra, full of grassland inhabited by deer, thickly grown with various trees and creepers full of fragrant flowers and fruits, where roam lions and tigers and proud elephants, a place that echoes with sounds of intoxicated birds and waterfalls.

338.sa: ततस्तं मारुतप्रख्यस्सहरिर्मारुतात्मजः।।4.67.40।। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः। वृतं नानाविधैः वृक्षैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्।।4.67.41।। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्। सिंहशार्दूलचरितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्।।4.67.42।। मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम्।
338.e: The son of Maruta, who was as eminent as the Windgod, the crusher of enemies ascended the great mountain Mahendra, full of grassland inhabited by deer, thickly grown with various trees and creepers full of fragrant flowers and fruits, where roam lions and tigers and proud elephants, a place that echoes with sounds of intoxicated birds and waterfalls.

338.sa: महद्भिरुच्छ्रितं शृङ्गैर्महेन्द्रं स महाबलः।।4.67.43।। विचचार हरिश्रेष्ठो महेन्द्रसमविक्रमः।
338.e: The mighty, preeminent monkey who was equal to Indra in valour took a leap from the high peaks of the tall mountain, Mahendra৷৷

338.sa: पादाभ्यां पीडितस्तेन महाशैलो महात्मना।।4.67.44।। रराज सिंहाभिहतो महान्मत्त इव द्विपः।
338.e: Crushed by the feet of the great self, Hanuman, the huge mountain looked like a proud elephant struck by a lion.

338.sa: मुमोच सलिलोत्पीडान्विप्रकीर्णशिलोच्चयः।।4.67.45।। वित्रस्तमृगमातङ्गः प्रकम्पितमहाद्रुमः।
338.e: The rocks of the mountain got scattered by the force. The deer and elephants were terrified. The trees were shaken up violently and streams of water gushed forth.

338.sa: नानागन्धर्वमिथुनैः पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः।।4.67.46।। उत्पतद्भिश्च विहगैर्विद्याधरगणैरपि। त्यज्यमानमहासानुस्सन्निलीनमहोरगः।।4.67.47।। चलशृङ्गशिलोद्घातस्तदाऽभूत्स महागिरिः।
338.e: Shaken by the rude shock, couples of intoxicated gandharvas left in a huff the vast slopes of the great mountain. Flocks of birds and groups of vidyadharas flew away. The serpents went into hiding. Rocks fell off the shaken mountain.

338.sa: नानागन्धर्वमिथुनैः पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः।।4.67.46।। उत्पतद्भिश्च विहगैर्विद्याधरगणैरपि। त्यज्यमानमहासानुस्सन्निलीनमहोरगः।।4.67.47।। चलशृङ्गशिलोद्घातस्तदाऽभूत्स महागिरिः।
338.e: Shaken by the rude shock, couples of intoxicated gandharvas left in a huff the vast slopes of the great mountain. Flocks of birds and groups of vidyadharas flew away. The serpents went into hiding. Rocks fell off the shaken mountain.

338.sa: निश्श्वसद्भिस्तदाऽर्तैस्तु भुजङ्गैरर्धनि:सृतैः।।4.67.48।। सपताक इवाभाति स तदा धरणीधरः।
338.e: The serpents with their bodies half protruded out of the rocks and hissing looked like flags planted on the mountain.

338.sa: ऋषिभिस्त्राससम्भ्रान्तैस्त्यज्यमानः शिलोच्चयः।।4.67.49।। सीदन्महति कान्तारे सार्थहीन इवाध्वगः।
338.e: The alarmed and agitated sages abandonned the mountain peaks.The mountain appeared like a lone traveller separated from the caravan in the great forest.

338.sa: सवेगवान् वेगसमाहितात्मा हरिप्रवीरः परवीरहन्ता। मनस्समाधाय महानुभावो जगाम लङ्कां मनसा मनस्वी।।4.67.50।।
338.e: Magnanimous, wise and heroic Hanuman, destroyer of enemy warriors, fixed his attention on speed, betook himself mentally to Lanka (ere he reached it physically). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामाणये वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyseventh sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

339.sa: ततो रावणनीतायाः सीतायाः शत्रुकर्शनः। इयेष पदमन्वेष्टुं चारणाचरिते पथि।।5.1.1।।
339.e: Hanuman, crusher of enemies resolved to find the whereabouts of Sita, carried away by Ravana. He followed the path of the Charanas, celestial bards.

339.sa: दुष्करं निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वं चिकीर्षन् कर्म वानरः। समुदग्रशिरोग्रीवो गवांपतिरिवाबभौ।।5.1.2।।
339.e: Hanuman who raised his head and neck, intending to cross the formidable ocean which none else could accomplish, looked like a leading bull.

339.sa: अथ वैडूर्यवर्णेषु शाद्वलेषु महाबलः। धीरः सलिलकल्पेषु विचचार यथासुखम्।।5.1.3।।
339.e: Tawnyhued Hanuman, gifted with extraordinary strength and patience happily strolled on the marshy tracts of grassy land which had the colour of vaidurya.

339.sa: द्विजान् वित्रासयन् धीमानुरसा पादपान् हरन्। मृगांश्च सुबहून्निघ्नन् प्रवृद्ध इव केसरी।।5.1.4।।
339.e: Wise Hanuman went about like a lion scaring away birds, uprooting trees with his chest, and trampling many animals.

339.sa: नीललोहितमांजिष्ठपत्रवर्णैः सितासितैः। स्वभावविहितैश्चित्रैर्धातुभिः समलङ्कृतम्।।5.1.5।। कामरूपिभिराविष्टमभीक्ष्णं सपरिच्छदैः। यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वैर्देवकल्पैश्च पन्नगैः।।5.1.6।।
339.e: The mountain was as though decorated with mineral rocks of varied colours like blue, red, yellow and green as well as black and white৷৷It was frequently visited  by yakshas, kinneras, gandharvas and nagas surrounded by their retinue, capable of assuming any form at their free will rivalling gods and nagas in splendour.

339.sa: नीललोहितमांजिष्ठपत्रवर्णैः सितासितैः। स्वभावविहितैश्चित्रैर्धातुभिः समलङ्कृतम्।।5.1.5।। कामरूपिभिराविष्टमभीक्ष्णं सपरिच्छदैः। यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वैर्देवकल्पैश्च पन्नगैः।।5.1.6।।
339.e: The mountain was as though decorated with mineral rocks of varied colours like blue, red, yellow and green as well as black and white৷৷It was frequently visited  by yakshas, kinneras, gandharvas and nagas surrounded by their retinue, capable of assuming any form at their free will rivalling gods and nagas in splendour.

339.sa: स तस्य गिरिवर्यस्य तले नागवरायुते। तिष्ठन् कपिवरस्तत्र ह्रदे नाग इवाबभौ।।5.1.7।।
339.e: As the monkey leader stood at the foot of the great mountain filled with lordly elephants he looked like an elephant standing at the centre of a pond.

339.sa: स सूर्याय महेन्द्राय पवनाय स्वयंभुवे। भूतेभ्यश्चाञ्जलिं कृत्वा चकार गमने मतिम्।।5.1.8।।
339.e: Offering salutations with folded palms to the Sungod, to Mahendra, lord of the gods, to the windgod, to the Creator Brahma and to all the attendants of lord Siva, made up his mind to proceed (to Lanka).

339.sa: अञ्जलिं प्राङ्मुखः कुर्वन् पवनायात्मयोनये। ततो हि ववृधे गन्तुं दक्षिणो दक्षिणां दिशम्।।5.1.9।।
339.e: Hanuman, endowed with great equanimity, facing the east and joining his palms by way of salutaion to the Windgod, his father, he enlarged his size and turned south in order to depart.

339.sa: प्लवङ्गप्रवरैर्दृष्टः प्लवने कृतनिश्चयः। ववृधे रामवृद्ध्यर्थं समुद्र इव पर्वसु।।5.1.10।।
339.e: Having made up his mind to leap for the cause of Rama, Hanuman began to grow in size just as the sea grows during the fullmoon and newmoon days, while the monkey troops were watching.

339.sa: निष्प्रमाणशरीरः सन् लिलङ्घयिषुरर्णवम्। बाहुभ्यां पीडयामास चरणाभ्यां च पर्वतम्।।5.1.11।।
339.e: Having swollen to an immeasurable figure, he pressed on the mountain with his feet and hands in an attempt to cross the ocean.

339.sa: स चचालाचलश्चापि मुहूर्तं कपिपीडितः। तरूणां पुष्पिताग्राणां सर्वं पुष्पमशातयत्।।5.1.12।।
339.e: Pressed firmly by Hanuman, the mountain was shaken for a moment which caused the flowers to drop down from the tree tops.

339.sa: तेन पादपमुक्तेन पुष्पौघेण सुगन्धिना। सर्वतः संवृतः शैलो बभौ पुष्पमयो यथा।।5.1.13।।
339.e: With heaps of flowers full of fragrance fallen down from the trees all over the mountain, it looked as though it was a mountain of flowers.

339.sa: तेन चोत्तमवीर्येण पीड्यमानः स पर्वतः। सलिलं सम्प्रसुस्राव मदं मत्त इव द्विपः।।5.1.14।।
339.e: The mountain pressed hard under the feet of the valiant (Hanuman), discharged streams of water just as an elephant in rut would exude water of intoxication.

339.sa: पीड्यमानस्तु बलिना महेन्द्रस्तेन पर्वतः। रीतीर्निर्वर्तयामास काञ्चनाञ्जनराजतीः।।5.1.15।।
339.e: Pressed by the powerful Hanuman, mount Mahendra let out streams of the hue of gold and silver (containing the ores of these minerals)৷৷

339.sa: मुमोच च शिलाः शैलो विशालाः समनःशिलाः। मध्यमेनार्चिषा जुष्टा धूमराजीरिवानलः।।5.1.16।।
339.e: The mountain threw down big boulders along with sulphur just like fire emits columns of smoke, surrounded by flames.

339.sa: गिरिणा पीड्यमानेन पीड्यमानानि सर्वतः। गुहाविष्टानि भूतानि विनेदुर्विकृतैः स्वरैः।।5.1.17।।
339.e: Squeezed on all sides of the mountain by Hanuman, all creatures living in the caves shrieked making horrible sounds .

339.sa: स महासत्त्वसन्नादः शैलपीडानिमित्तजः। पृथिवीं पूरयामास दिशश्चोपवनानि च।।5.1.18।।
339.e: Due to the crushing of the mountain, a loud noise of the various creatures shot up filling the earth in all directions and groves around.

339.sa: शिरोभिः पृथुभिः सर्पा व्यक्तस्वस्तिकलक्षणैः। वमन्तः पावकं घोरं ददंशुर्दशनैः शिलाः।।5.1.19।।
339.e: The snakes spread out their broad hoods manifesting swastika marks on them and bit the rocks with their fangs pouring out terrible fire.

339.sa: तास्तदा सविषैर्दष्टाः कुपितैस्तैर्महाशिलाः। जज्ज्वलुः पावकोद्दीप्ता बिभिदुश्च सहस्रधा।।5.1.20।।
339.e: Bitten by the venomous and angry snakes, the mountain was broken into a thousand pieces by the blazing flames.

339.sa: यानि चौषधजालानि तस्मिन् जातानि पर्वते। विषघ्नान्यपि नागानां न शेकुः शमितुं विषम्।।5.1.21।।
339.e: Even the medicinal herbs grown on the mountain could not neutralize the effect of the poison of snakes.

339.sa: भिद्यतेऽयं गिरिर्भूतैरिति मत्त्वा तपस्विनः। त्रस्ता विद्याधरास्तस्मादुत्पेतुः स्त्री गणैः सह।।5.1.22।। पानभूमिगतं हित्वा हैममासवभाजनम्। पात्राणि च महार्हाणि करकांश्च हिरण्मयान्।।5.1.23। लेह्यानुच्चावचान् भक्ष्यान् मांसानि विविधानि च। आर्षभाणि च चर्माणि खडगांश्च कनकत्सरून्।।5.1.24।।
339.e: Even the ascetics left the place approaching that the mountain would be broken into pieces by creatures. The alarmed vidyadharas leaped into the sky along with groups of their women, leaving behind golden jugs of wine as well as precious utensils, big and small sizes, and golden goblets, cups in the drinking place, as well as many tasty eatables like licking food, chewing food and many types of meat. They also left bullhides and swords with golden sheaths.

339.sa: भिद्यतेऽयं गिरिर्भूतैरिति मत्त्वा तपस्विनः। त्रस्ता विद्याधरास्तस्मादुत्पेतुः स्त्री गणैः सह।।5.1.22।। पानभूमिगतं हित्वा हैममासवभाजनम्। पात्राणि च महार्हाणि करकांश्च हिरण्मयान्।।5.1.23। लेह्यानुच्चावचान् भक्ष्यान् मांसानि विविधानि च। आर्षभाणि च चर्माणि खडगांश्च कनकत्सरून्।।5.1.24।।
339.e: Even the ascetics left the place approaching that the mountain would be broken into pieces by creatures. The alarmed vidyadharas leaped into the sky along with groups of their women, leaving behind golden jugs of wine as well as precious utensils, big and small sizes, and golden goblets, cups in the drinking place, as well as many tasty eatables like licking food, chewing food and many types of meat. They also left bullhides and swords with golden sheaths.

339.sa: भिद्यतेऽयं गिरिर्भूतैरिति मत्त्वा तपस्विनः। त्रस्ता विद्याधरास्तस्मादुत्पेतुः स्त्री गणैः सह।।5.1.22।। पानभूमिगतं हित्वा हैममासवभाजनम्। पात्राणि च महार्हाणि करकांश्च हिरण्मयान्।।5.1.23। लेह्यानुच्चावचान् भक्ष्यान् मांसानि विविधानि च। आर्षभाणि च चर्माणि खडगांश्च कनकत्सरून्।।5.1.24।।
339.e: Even the ascetics left the place approaching that the mountain would be broken into pieces by creatures. The alarmed vidyadharas leaped into the sky along with groups of their women, leaving behind golden jugs of wine as well as precious utensils, big and small sizes, and golden goblets, cups in the drinking place, as well as many tasty eatables like licking food, chewing food and many types of meat. They also left bullhides and swords with golden sheaths.

339.sa: कृतकण्ठगुणाः क्षीबा रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनाः। रक्ताक्षाः पुष्कराक्षाश्च गगनं प्रतिपेदिरे।।5.1.25।।
339.e: The intoxicated vidyadharas with eyes red like lotuses, wearing garlands around the neck and smeared with red sandalpaste flew into the sky.

339.sa: हारनूपुरकेयूरपारिहार्यधराः स्त्रियः। विस्मिताः सस्मितास्तस्थुराकाशे रमणैः सह।।5.1.26।।
339.e: Adorned with necklaces, anklets and armlets, the vidyadharis stayed wonderstruck in the sky, smiling gently in the company of their lovers.

339.sa: दर्शयन्तो महाविद्यां विद्याधरमहर्षयः। सहितास्तस्थुराकाशे वीक्षाञ्चक्रुश्च पर्वतम्।।5.1.27।।
339.e: The seers among the Vidyadharas, proficient in different fields of knowledge were also watching the mountain from the sky along with others.

339.sa: शुश्रुवुश्च तदा शब्दमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्। चारणानां च सिद्धानां स्थितानां विमलेऽम्बरे।।5.1.28।।
339.e: Then the vidyadharas heard the words of praise(of Hanuman) by the sages, seekers of the ultimate truth, the charanas and the siddhas who stood and watched in the clear sky:

339.sa: एष पर्वतसङ्काशो हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। तितीर्षति महावेगस्समुद्रं मकरालयम्।।5.1.29।।
339.e: "Hanuman the son of the Windgod, who is like a mountain, with extraordinary might  intends to cross the ocean, the abode of crocodiles".

339.sa: रामार्थं वानरार्थं च चिकीर्षन् कर्म दुष्करम्। समुद्रस्य परं पारं दुष्प्रापं प्राप्तुमिच्छति।।5.1.30।।
339.e: "For the sake of Rama and the vanaras he wants to reach the other shore of the ocean, which is difficult, and indeed impossible".

339.sa: इति विद्याधराः श्रुत्वा वचस्तेषां महात्मनाम्। तमप्रमेयं ददृशुः पर्वते वानरर्षभम्।।5.1.31।।
339.e: The vidyadharas heard the sages speaking in that manner on the mountain. They beheld Hanuman, the bull among vanaras, whose strength  was beyond measure.

339.sa: दुधुवे च स रोमाणि चकम्पे चाचलोपमः। ननाद सुमहानादं सुमहानिव तोयदः।।5.1.32।।
339.e: Hanuman, huge as a mountain moved his body and shook the hair on his body, thundering like a cloud.

339.sa: आनुपूर्व्येण वृत्तं च लाङ्गूलं लोमभिश्चितम्। उत्पतिष्यन् विचिक्षेप पक्षिराज इवोरगम्।।5.1.33।।
339.e: Like the king of birds Garuda would shake a serpent, he shook his tail covered with hair in order to take off.

339.sa: तस्य लाङ्गूलमाविद्धमात्तवेगस्य पृष्ठतः। ददृशे गरुडेनेव ह्रियमाणो महोरगः।।5.1.34।।
339.e: Hanuman had the tail curled at his back which appeared like a big serpent being carried off by Garuda.

339.sa: बाहू संस्तम्भयामास महापरिघसन्निभौ। ससाद च कपिः कट्यां चरणौ सञ्चुकोच च।।5.1.35।।
339.e: The monkey fixed his arms, looking like iron clubs, firmly on the mountain and crouched his waist and contracted his feet.

339.sa: संहृत्य च भुजौ श्रीमांस्तथैव च शिरोधराम्। तेजः सत्त्वं तथा वीर्यमाविवेश स वीर्यवान्।।5.1.36।।
339.e: The glorious and courageous Hanuman his head and shoulders contracted, summoned up all his energy and vigour.

339.sa: मार्गमालोकयन्दूरादूर्ध्वं प्रणिहितेक्षणः। रुरोध हृदये प्राणानाकाशमवलोकयन्।।5.1.37।।
339.e: Having cast his eyes upward in order to view the distance and direction in which he had to leap, he restrained his breath in the chest while looking at the sky.

339.sa: पद्भ्यां दृढमवस्थानं कृत्वा स कपिकुञ्जरः। निकुञ्च्य कर्णौ हनुमानुत्पतिष्यन् महाबलः।। वानरान् वानरश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।5.1.38।।
339.e: A mighty elephant among vanaras, Hanuman holding his feet firmly and standing in that position, contracted his ears and addressed the monkeys, when he was about to leap:

339.sa: यथा राघवनिर्मुक्तः शरः श्वसनविक्रमः। गच्छेत्तद्वद्गमिष्यामि लङ्कां रावणपालिताम्।।5.1.39।।
339.e: "Just like an arrow released by Raghava would fly, I too will proceed with the speed of the wind to reach Lanka ruled by Ravana.

339.sa: न हि द्रक्ष्यामि यदि तां लङ्कायां जनकात्मजाम्। अनेनैव हि वेगेन गमिष्यामि सुरालयम्।।5.1.40।।
339.e: "If I am not able to find the  daughter of Janaka at Lanka I will go to heaven, abode of the gods, with the same speed.

339.sa: यदि वा त्रिदिवे सीतां न द्रक्ष्याम्यकृतश्रमः। बद्ध्वा राक्षसराजानमानयिष्यामि रावणम्।।5.1.41।।
339.e: "If I do not find Sita in heaven in spite of my efforts, I will bind that king of demons, Ravana and bring him here.

339.sa: सर्वथा कृतकार्योऽहमेष्यामि सह सीतया। आनयिष्यामि वा लङ्कां समुत्पाट्य सरावणाम्।।5.1.42।।
339.e: "I will, by all means return successful with Sita or else I will uproot Lanka along with Ravana and bring him here".

339.sa: एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमान्वानरान्वानरोत्तमः।।5.1.43।। उत्पपाताथ वेगेन वेगवानविचारयन्। सुपर्णमिव चात्मानं मेने स कपिकुञ्जरः।।5.1.44।।
339.e: Having thus addressed the monkeys the foremost of vanaras,Hanuman endowed with great speed leaped without any exertion. The elephant among monkeys felt like Garuda.

339.sa: एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमान्वानरान्वानरोत्तमः।।5.1.43।। उत्पपाताथ वेगेन वेगवानविचारयन्। सुपर्णमिव चात्मानं मेने स कपिकुञ्जरः।।5.1.44।।
339.e: Having thus addressed the monkeys the foremost of vanaras,Hanuman endowed with great speed leaped without any exertion. The elephant among monkeys felt like Garuda.

339.sa: समुत्पतति तस्मिंस्तु वेगात्ते नगरोहिणः। संहृत्य विटपान् सर्वान् समुत्पेतुः समन्ततः।।5.1.45।।
339.e: When he took off, numerous trees on the mountain drawing together the branches all over flew along with him.

339.sa: स मत्तकोयष्टिमकान् पादपान् पुष्पशालिनः। उद्वहन्नूरुवेगेन जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे।।5.1.46।।
339.e: He swept away the lapwings in heat on the blossoms of the trees by the speed of his thighs while he coursed through the cloudless sky.

339.sa: ऊरुवेगोद्धता वृक्षा मुहूर्तं कपिमन्वयुः। प्रस्थितं दीर्घमध्वानं स्वबन्धुमिव बान्धवाः।।5.1.47।।
339.e: Swept away by the force of his thighs, the trees bent forward following him for a while just as relatives accompany their kith and kin on long travel.

339.sa: तमूरुवेगोन्मथिताः सालाश्चान्ये नगोत्तमाः। अनुजग्मुर्हनूमन्तं सैन्या इव महीपतिम्।।5.1.48।।
339.e: Uprooted by the force of Hanuman's thighs,great trees like  sala followed him just like the troops follow the king.

339.sa: सुपुष्पिताग्रैर्बहुभिः पादपैरन्वितः कपिः। हनुमान् पर्वताकारो बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः।।5.1.49।।
339.e: With numerous trees laden with flowers following him, Hanuman who looked like a mountain, presented a queer spectable.

339.sa: सारवन्तोऽथ ये वृक्षा न्यमज्जन् लवणाम्भसि। भयादिव महेन्द्रस्य पर्वता वरुणालये।।5.1.50।।
339.e: Then the huge trees sank into the ocean of salt water even as mountains did, afraid of Indra's (thunderbolt).

339.sa: स नानाकुसुमैः कीर्णः कपिः साङ्कुरकोरकैः। शुशुभे मेघसङ्काशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः।।5.1.51।।
339.e: Covered with tender sprouts and buds of different kinds of flowers Hanuman shone brightly like a flying mountain with fireflies.

339.sa: विमुक्तास्तस्य वेगेन मुक्त्वा पुष्पाणि ते द्रुमाः। अवशीर्यन्त सलिले निवृत्ताः सुहृदो यथा।।5.1.52।।
339.e: Shedding their blossoms (under his thrust) the trees dropped into the waters of the sea just like close relatives follow at the time of farewell.

339.sa: लघुत्वेनोपपन्नं तद्विचित्रं सागरेऽपतत्। द्रुमाणां विविधं पुष्पं कपिवायुसमीरितम्।।5.1.53।। ताराचितमिवाकाशं प्रबभौ स महार्णवः।
339.e: Driven by the wind caused by Hanuman's speed a variety of flowers fell into the ocean because of their light weight and the ocean looked colourful and bright like the starspangled sky.

339.sa: पुष्पौघेणानुबद्धेन नानावर्णेन वानरः। बभौ मेघ इवाकाशे विद्युद्गण विभूषितः।।5.1.54।।
339.e: Covered with blossoms of different kinds and colours, Hanuman looked like a cloud brightened by lightnings in the sky.

339.sa: तस्य वेगसमाधूतैः पुष्पैस्तोयमदृश्यत।।5.1.55।। ताराभिरभिरामाभिरुदिताभिरिवाम्बरम्।
339.e: The seawater looked splendid with flowers dropped by dint of his speed. It  resembled the firmament spangled with enchanting stars just risen in the sky.

339.sa: तस्याम्बरगतौ बाहू ददृशाते प्रसारितौ।।5.1.56।। पर्वताग्राद्विनिष्क्रान्तौ पञ्चास्याविव पन्नगौ।
339.e: That great Vanara appeared as if he was gulping the entire ocean with its rising waves. While he was looking upward it appeared as though he was keen to drink in the sea as well.

339.sa: पिबन्निव बभौ चापि सोर्मिमालं महार्णवम्।।5.1.57।। पिपासुरिव चाकाशं ददृशे स महाकपिः।
339.e: While he was looking upward, that great vanara appeared as if, parched with thirst, he was gulping the entire ocean with its rising waves.

339.sa: तस्य विद्युत्प्रभाकारे वायुमार्गानुसारिणः।।5.1.58।। नयने विप्रकाशेते पर्वतस्थाविवानलौ।
339.e: As he was moving in the sky following the direction of the wind, his eyes blazed like two fires burning on the mountain, flashing like lightning.

339.sa: पिङ्गे पिङ्गाक्षमुख्यस्य बृहती परिमण्डले।।5.1.59।। चक्षुषी सम्प्राकाशेते चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ।
339.e: The large, round, reddishbrown eyes of Hanuman shed their bright light like the rising Moon and Sun.

339.sa: मुखं नासिकया तस्य ताम्रया ताम्रमाबभौ।।5.1.60।। सन्ध्यया समभिस्पृष्टं यथा तत्सूर्यमण्डलम्।
339.e: By the reflection of his copperyred nose, his face looked red like the Sun's orb coming close at twilight.

339.sa: लाङ्गूलं च समाविद्धं प्लवमानस्य शोभते।।5.1.61।। अम्बरे वायुपुत्रस्य शक्रध्वज इवोच्छ्रितम्।
339.e: As the son of the Windgod was flying through the sky, his coiled up tail looked splendid like the banner installed at the festival in honour of Indra (on the fifteenth day of the month of Bhadrapada).

339.sa: लाङ्गूलचक्रेण महान् शुक्लदंष्ट्रोऽनिलात्मजः।।5.1.62।। व्यरोचत महाप्राज्ञः परिवेषीव भास्करः।
339.e: With his white teeth and curled up tail, the wise son of the Windgod looked splendid like the halo of the Sungod.

339.sa: स्फिग्देशेनाभिताम्रेण रराज स महाकपिः।।5.1.63।। महता दारितेनेव गिरिर्गैरिकधातुना।
339.e: The great monkey with copperred buttocks (other parts being dark) looked splendid like a cleft mountain with a huge deposit of minerals shining red.

339.sa: तस्य वानरसिंहस्य प्लवमानस्य सागरम्।।5.1.64।। कक्षान्तरगतो वायुर्जीमूत इव गर्जति।
339.e: The wind passing through the arm pits of the lionlike vanara crossing the ocean sounded like a thundering cloud.

339.sa: खे यथा निपतत्युल्का ह्युत्तरान्ताद्विनिःसृता।।5.1.65।। दृश्यते सानुबन्धा च तथा स कपिकुञ्जरः।
339.e: The elephantlike monkey was seen darting across the ocean(going from north to south) like a meteor risen in the north  along with its tailend falling down the sky.

339.sa: पतत्पतङ्गसङ्काशो व्यायतः शुशुभे कपिः।।5.1.66।। प्रवृद्ध इव मातङ्गः कक्ष्यया बध्यमानया।
339.e: The vanara expanded into an enormous size form appeared as though moving like the setting Sun. He looked like a huge elephant bound round the waist.

339.sa: उपरिष्टाच्छरीरेण छायया चावगाढया।।5.1.67।। सागरे मारुताविष्टा नौरिवासीत्तदा कपिः।
339.e: When the vanara was flying in the sky, his shadow reflected in the ocean looked like a ship driven by the wind and sailing on the sea below (as if the lower part of his body was under water and upper part occupied the sky)

339.sa: यं यं देशं समुद्रस्य जगाम स महाकपिः। स स तस्योरुवेगेन सोन्माद इव लक्ष्यते।।5.1.68।।
339.e: Whichever part of the sea over which that monkey flew, it appeared as though it was riotous with eddies, whirlpools and revolving foam etc., stirred up by the speed of his thighs.

339.sa: सागरस्योर्मिजालानामुरसा शैलवर्ष्मणाम्। अभिघ्नंस्तु महावेगः पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः।।5.1.69।।
339.e: As the great vanara was flying swiftly, the oceanic waves in rows dashing against his chest rose as high as the  mountain.

339.sa: कपिवातश्च बलवान् मेघवातश्च निःसृतः। सागरं भीमनिर्घोषं कम्पयामासतुर्भृशम्।।5.1.70।।
339.e: The forceful wind generated by the monkey moving swiftly, and by the clouds agitated the ocean violently, creating dreadful sounds.

339.sa: विकर्षन्नूर्मिजालानि बृहन्ति लवणाम्भसि। पुप्लुवे कपिशार्दूलो विकिरन्निव रोदसी।।5.1.71।।
339.e: As the tiger among the monkeys pushed the big network of waves of the saltwater ocean and leaped forward, it appeared as if  he was drawing the intermediary space dividing the earth and the sky.

339.sa: मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशानुद्धतान् स महार्णवे। अत्यक्रामन्महावेगस्तरङ्गान् गणयन्निव।।5.1.72।।
339.e: Hanuman moving along in high speed looked as if he was counting the mighty waves risen ike Meru and Mandara mountains.

339.sa: तस्य वेगसमुद्धूतं जलं सजलदं तदा। अम्बरस्थं विबभ्राज शारदाभ्रमिवाततम्।।5.1.73।।
339.e: Then the water raised by his onrush along with the cloud widely spread in the sky shone like an outstreched autumnal cloud.

339.sa: तिमिनक्रझषाः कूर्मा दृश्यन्ते विवृतास्तदा। वस्त्रापकर्षणेनेव शरीराणि शरीरिणाम्।।5.1.74।।
339.e: On account of the seawater rising up,  the whales, crocodiles, fish and tortoises laid bare like the limbs of the body disrobed.

339.sa: प्लवमानं समीक्ष्याथ भुजङ्गाः सागरालयाः। व्योम्नि तं कपिशार्दूलं सुपर्ण इति मेनिरे।।5.1.75।।
339.e: Seeing Hanuman, the tiger among vanaras, coursing through the sky the serpents in their seaabode mistook him for Garuda.

339.sa: दशयोजनविस्तीर्णा त्रिंशद्योजनमायता। छाया वानरसिंहस्य जले चारुतराभवत्।।5.1.76।।
339.e: The shadow of Hanuman, the lion among monkeys, thirty yojanas long and ten yojanas in breadth appeared more pleasing৷৷

339.sa: श्वेताभ्रघनराजीव वायुपुत्रानुगामिनी। तस्य सा शुशुभे छाया वितता लवणाम्भसि।।5.1.77।।
339.e: The broad shadow of the son of the Windgod in the sea following him shone like a dark row of clouds sailing in the pristine sky.

339.sa: शुशुभे स महातेजा महाकायो महाकपिः। वायुमार्गे निरालम्बे पक्षवानिव पर्वतः।।5.1.78।।
339.e: Hanuman the great vanara, splendid with a huge body coursing through the air seemed like a winged mountain flying the sky without any support.

339.sa: येनासौ याति बलवान् वेगेन कपिकुञ्जरः। तेन मार्गेण सहसा द्रोणीकृत इवार्णवः।।5.1.79।।
339.e: As the powerful monkey, an elephant among vanaras, was proceeding swiftly along, the ocean got instantly transformed into a trough on account of water swelling by the force of his flight.

339.sa: आपाते पक्षिसङ्घानां पक्षिराज इव व्रजन्। हनुमान् मेघजालानि प्रकर्षन् मारुतो यथा।।5.1.80।।
339.e: Hanuman was found pulling clusters of big clouds along with him like the Windgod and appeared like Garuda,the king of birds, drawing flocks of birds along with him at the time of landing.

339.sa: पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि नीलमाञ्जिष्ठकानि च। कपिनाकृष्यमाणानि महाभ्राणि चकाशिरे।।5.1.81।।
339.e: While Hanuman was drawing big clouds which were either white or red or blue or yellow, he looked charming.

339.sa: प्रविशन्नभ्रजालानि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः। प्रच्छन्नश्च प्रकाशश्च चन्द्रमा इव लक्ष्यते।।5.1.82।।
339.e: Entering into and emerging from the clouds, he looked like the Moon that appears and disappears (behind a bank of clouds).

339.sa: प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा प्लवङ्गं त्वरितं तदा। ववर्षुः पुष्पवर्षाणि देवगन्धर्वदानवाः।।5.1.83।।
339.e: Then seeing Hanuman crossing quickly, the gods, gandharvas and demons rained flowers on him.

339.sa: तताप न हि तं सूर्यः प्लवन्तं वानरोत्तमम्। सिषेवे च तदा वायू रामकार्यार्थसिद्धये।।5.1.84।।
339.e: The Sun spared Hanuman from the heat and even the Windgod served him, blowing cool while he was taking leaps in order to fulfil Rama's mission.

339.sa: ऋषयस्तुष्टुवुश्चैनं प्लवमानं विहायसा। जगुश्च देवगन्धर्वाः प्रशंसन्तो महौजसम्।।5.1.85।।
339.e: The sages praised him while he was coursing through the sky, the gods and gandharvas sang in praise of him extolling his majesty and vigour.

339.sa: नागाश्च तुष्टुवुर्यक्षा रक्षांसि विबुधाः खगाः। प्रेक्ष्य सर्वे कपिवरं सहसा विगतक्लमम्।।5.1.86।।
339.e: Observing the unwearied monkey the nagas, yakshas, the demons (protecting the southwest), the learned sages and birds praised him.

339.sa: तस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूले प्लवमाने हनूमति। इक्ष्वाकुकुलमानार्थी चिन्तयामास सागरः।।5.1.87।।
339.e: While the monkeychief was leaping (across the sea) the Seagod wished the wellbeing of the Ikshvaku family and honoured him. (The Seagod belonged to the same race) :

339.sa: साहाय्यं वानरेन्द्रस्य यदि नाहं हनूमत:। करिष्यामि भविष्यामि सर्ववाच्यो विवक्षताम्।।5.1.88।।
339.e: 'If I fail to help the monkeychief, the wise will blame me'.

339.sa: अहमिक्ष्वाकुनाथेन सगरेण विवर्धितः। इक्ष्वाकुसचिवश्चायं नावसीदितुमर्हति।।5.1.89।।
339.e: 'I expanded on account of a scion of the Ikshvaku race (Sagara) and I should not do anything to make him (Hanuman) suffer since he is the minister helping the Ikshvaku race'.

339.sa: तथा मया विधातव्यं विश्रमेत यथा कपिः।।5.1.90।। शेषं च मयि विश्रान्तः सुखेनातिपतिष्यति।
339.e: 'I will have to make arrangements for his rest. Later he can resume his journey comfortably'.

339.sa: इति कृत्वा मतिं साध्वींसमुद्र श्छन्नमम्भसि।।5.1.91।। हिरण्यनाभं मैनाकमुवाच गिरिसत्तमम्।
339.e: Having resolved in his mind, the Seagod addressed the noble, golden mount Mainaka, hidden in the sea:

339.sa: त्वमिहासुरसंघानां पातालतलवासिनाम्।।5.1.92।। देवराज्ञा गिरिश्रेष्ठ परिघः सन्निवेशितः।
339.e: 'O foremost mountain you are kept here by Indra, lord of the gods as a barrier against the intrusion of demons residing in the netherworld.

339.sa: त्वमेषां जातवीर्याणां पुनरेवोत्पतिष्यताम्।।5.1.93।। पातालस्याप्रमेयस्य द्वारमावृत्य तिष्ठसि।
339.e: "You are staying at the entrance preventing the violent demons of the immeasurable nether world from jumping onto the surface.

339.sa: तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव शक्तिस्ते शैल वर्धितुम्।।5.1.94।। तस्मात्संचोदयामि त्वामुत्तिष्ठ गिरिसत्तम।
339.e: "O noble mountain you have the capacity to grow across, upward and downward by your free will. I therefore prompt you to grow.

339.sa: स एष कपिशार्दूलस्त्वामुपर्येति वीर्यवान्।।5.1.95।। हनूमान्रामकार्यार्थं भीमकर्मा खमाप्लुतः।
339.e: "Valiant Hanuman, a tiger among monkeys and a performer of dreadful deeds, is  flying over you to fulfil Rama's mission

339.sa: अस्य साह्यं मया कार्यमिक्ष्वाकुकुलवर्तिनः।।5.1.96।। मम हीक्ष्वाकवः पूज्याः परं पूज्यतमास्तव।
339.e: "I should help him for he is working for the welfare of the Ikshavaku family. The Ikshvaku kings are worthy of adoration to me and for you as well.

339.sa: कुरु साचिव्यमस्माकं न नः कार्यमतिक्रमेत्।।5.1.97।। कर्तव्यमकृतं कार्यं सतां मन्युमुदीरयेत्।
339.e: "You may act as our minister and let us not miss this chance. Pious men lose their cool if a worthy act is left unfulfilled.

339.sa: सलिलादूर्ध्वमुत्तिष्ठ तिष्ठत्वेष कपिस्त्वयि।।5.1.98।। अस्माकमतिथिश्चैव पूज्यश्च प्लवतां वरः।
339.e: "Rise up from the waters. Let him rest on you since this noble monkey is our guest and worthy of worship.

339.sa: चामीकरमहानाभ देवगन्धर्वसेवित।।5.1.99।। हनुमांस्त्वयि विश्रान्तस्ततः शेषं गमिष्यति।
339.e: "O goldenpeaked mountainyou are the refuge of the gods and gandharvas. Let him also rest on you for a while before he negotiates the remaining part of the journey.

339.sa: काकुत्स्थस्यानृशंस्यं च मैथिल्याश्च विवासनम्।।5.1.100।। श्रमं च प्लवगेन्द्रस्य समीक्ष्योत्थातुमर्हसि।
339.e: "You ought to rise up if you consider the nobility of the scion of the Kakusthas, the deportation of Mythili, and the exertion put forth by Hanuman, the lord of monkeys".

339.sa: हिरण्यनाभो मैनाको निशम्य लवणाम्भसः।।5.1.101।। उत्पपात जलात्तूर्णं महाद्रुमलतायुतः।
339.e: Hearing the command of the god of the ocean, mount Mainaka, rich in gold and covered with trees and creepers rose up at once from the water.

339.sa: स सागरजलं भित्त्वा बभूवाभ्युत्थितस्तदा।।5.1.102।। यथा जलधरं भित्त्वा दीप्तरश्मिर्दिवाकरः।
339.e: Just as the rising Sun comes out with glowing rays tearing the veil of dark clouds, the mountain rose up from the water of the ocean.

339.sa: स महात्मा मुहूर्तेन सर्वतः सलिलावृतः।।5.1.103।। दर्शयामास शृङ्गाणि सागरेण नियोजितः। आदित्योदयसङ्काशैरालिखद्भिरिवाम्बरम्। शातकुम्भमयैः शृङ्गैः सकिन्नरमहोरगैः।।5.1.104।।
339.e: At the instance of Varuna, (the presiding deity of the ocean) the lofty mountain appeared, projecting its peaks, hitherto submerged in the water. The golden peaks inhabited by nagas and kinnaras resemmbled the rising Sun as though scraping the sky in a moment.

339.sa: स महात्मा मुहूर्तेन सर्वतः सलिलावृतः।।5.1.103।। दर्शयामास शृङ्गाणि सागरेण नियोजितः। आदित्योदयसङ्काशैरालिखद्भिरिवाम्बरम्। शातकुम्भमयैः शृङ्गैः सकिन्नरमहोरगैः।।5.1.104।।
339.e: At the instance of Varuna, (the presiding deity of the ocean) the lofty mountain appeared, projecting its peaks, hitherto submerged in the water. The golden peaks inhabited by nagas and kinnaras resemmbled the rising Sun as though scraping the sky in a moment.

339.sa: तप्तजाम्बूनदैः शृङ्गैः पर्वतस्य समुत्थितैः।।5.1.105।। आकाशं शस्त्रसङ्काशमभवत्काञ्चनप्रभम्।
339.e: The sky shone like barnished weapons smeared with the golden colour of the mountain peaks that rose up above the water.

339.sa: जातरूपमयैः शृङ्गैर्भ्राजमानैः स्वयंप्रभैः।।5.1.106।। आदित्यशतसङ्काशः सोऽभवद्गिरिसत्तमः।
339.e: The noble mountain, Mainaka was glittering  like a thousand Suns with selfeffulgent golden peaks shining.

339.sa: तमुत्थितमसङ्गेन हनुमानग्रतः स्थितम्।।5.1.107।। मध्ये लवणतोयस्य विघ्नोऽयमिति निश्चितः।
339.e: Hanuman considered the mountain rising up in the midst of the ocean and standing in front an impediment.

339.sa: स तमुच्छ्र्रतमत्यर्थं महावेगो महाकपिः।।5.1.108।। उरसा पातयामास जीमूतमिव मारुतः।
339.e: The great vanara,who was swift in action felled down the mountain that had risen high instantly with his chest just as the wind would strike a cloud.

339.sa: स तथा पातितस्तेन कपिना पर्वतोत्तमः।।5.1.109।। बुद्ध्वा तस्य कपेर्वेगं जहर्ष च ननन्द च।
339.e: Felled by the vanara's speed, the tall mountain overwhelmed with joy roared in high pitch.

339.sa: तमाकाशगतं वीरमाकाशे समुपस्थितः।।5.1.110।। प्रीतो हृष्टमाना वाक्यमब्रवीत्पर्वतः कपिम्। मानुषं धारयन् रूपमात्मनः शिखरे स्थितः।।5.1.111।।
339.e: Now the mountain assumed a human form  and standing on its own summit, which stood very high, and glad at heart, addressed the heroic vanara gone to the aerial region.

339.sa: तमाकाशगतं वीरमाकाशे समुपस्थितः।।5.1.110।। प्रीतो हृष्टमाना वाक्यमब्रवीत्पर्वतः कपिम्। मानुषं धारयन् रूपमात्मनः शिखरे स्थितः।।5.1.111।।
339.e: Now the mountain assumed a human form  and standing on its own summit, which stood very high, and glad at heart, addressed the heroic vanara gone to the aerial region.

339.sa: दुष्करं कृतवान्कर्म त्वमिदं वानरोत्तम। निपत्य मम शृङ्गेषु विश्रमस्व यथासुखम्।।5.1.112।।
339.e: "O best of vanaras you have achieved a formidable deed. Alighting on my peak and comfortably resting awhile, you may resume your journey.

339.sa: राघवस्य कुले जातैरुदधिः परिवर्धितः। स त्वां रामहिते युक्तं प्रत्यर्चयति सागरः।।5.1.113।।
339.e: "The son of Rama's family, Sagara, has extended the ocean in the past.It is most appropriate that he (the god of the sea) honours you in return as you have set out in the service of Rama.

339.sa: कृते च प्रतिकर्तव्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः। सोऽयं त्वत्प्रतिकारार्थी त्वत्तः सम्मानमर्हति।।5.1.114।।
त्वन्निमित्तमनेनाहं बहुमानात्प्रचोदितः। तिष्ठ त्वं कपिशार्दूल मयि विश्रम्य गम्यताम्।।5.1.115।। तव सानुषु विश्रान्तः शेषं प्रक्रमतामिति। योजनानां शतं चापि कपिरेष समाप्लुतः।।5.1.116।।
339.e: "I was prompted by the ocean for your sake since he has great regard for you. O great monkey you may rest here for a while and continue your journey. The lord of the ocean feels that this tiger among monkeys can cover the distance of a hundred yojanas. He tells me, 'let him rest on your peak and then cover the rest of the distance'.

339.sa: त्वन्निमित्तमनेनाहं बहुमानात्प्रचोदितः। तिष्ठ त्वं कपिशार्दूल मयि विश्रम्य गम्यताम्।।5.1.115।। तव सानुषु विश्रान्तः शेषं प्रक्रमतामिति। योजनानां शतं चापि कपिरेष समाप्लुतः।।5.1.116।।
339.e: "I was prompted by the ocean for your sake since he has great regard for you. O great monkey you may rest here for a while and continue your journey. The lord of the ocean feels that this tiger among monkeys can cover the distance of a hundred yojanas. He tells me, 'let him rest on your peak and then cover the rest of the distance'.

339.sa: तदिदं गन्धवत्स्वादु कन्दमूलफलं बहु। तदास्वाद्य हरिश्रेष्ठ विश्रान्तोऽनु गमिष्यसि।।5.1.117।।
339.e: "O foremost of the monkeys after eating plenty of sweet and tasty roots and fruits and resting a while you may go.

339.sa: अस्माकमपि सम्बन्ध: कपिमुख्य त्वयास्ति वै। प्रख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु महागुणपरिग्रहः।।5.1.118।।
339.e: "O chief of monkeys, indeed we too have a relationship with you based on merit  which is wellknown to all the three worlds.

339.sa: वेगवन्तः प्लवन्तो ये प्लवगा मारुतात्मज। तेषां मुख्यतमं मन्ये त्वामहं कपिकुञ्जर।।5.1.119।।
339.e: "O son of the Windgod you are an elephant among monkeys, the foremost among them who move at a high speed.

339.sa: अतिथिः किल पूजार्हः प्राकृतोऽपि विजानता। धर्मं जिज्ञासमानेन किं पुनस्त्वादृशो महान्।।5.1.120।।
339.e: "Even a newcomer, however ordinary, deserves worship by a wise man who wishes to educate himself in the path of righteousness. Needless to say that distinguished guest like you deserves all reverence.

339.sa: त्वं हि देववरिष्ठस्य मारुतस्य महात्मनः। पुत्रस्तस्यैव वेगेन सदृशः कपिकुञ्जर।।5.1.121।।
339.e: "O foremost among the vanaras you are the son of the highsouled Windgod's, preeminent among the gods, you are also equal to him in speed.

339.sa: पूजिते त्वयि धर्मज्ञ पूजां प्राप्नोति मारुतः। तस्मात्त्वं पूजनीयो मे शृणु चाप्यत्र कारणम्।।5.1.122।।
339.e: "O knower of righteousness to worship you is to honour the Windgod. Therefore you are worthy of worship for me. I will tell you the reason. Listen.

339.sa: पूर्वं कृतयुगे तात पर्वताः पक्षिणोऽभवन्। ते हि जग्मुर्दिशः सर्वा गरुडानिलवेगिनः।।5.1.123।।
339.e: "Formerly in Kritayuga, O dear, mountains were endowed with wings. They used to move speedily in all directions like Garuda and the Windgod.

339.sa: ततस्तेषु प्रयातेषु देवसङ्घा: महर्षिभिः। भूतानि च भयं जग्मुस्तेषां पतनशङ्कया।5.1.124।।
339.e: "When they moved about, even hosts of sages, gods and creatures panicked for fear of falling down (and destroying all worlds).

339.sa: ततः क्रुद्धः सहस्राक्षः पर्वतानां शतक्रतुः। पक्षान् चिच्छेद वज्रेण तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः।।5.1.125।।
339.e: "Provoked at this, the thousandeyed Indra who had performed a hundred sacrifices cut off the wings of mountains into a thousands pieces with his thunderbolt.

339.sa: स मामुपागतः क्रुद्धो वज्रमुद्यम्य देवराट्। ततोऽहं सहसा क्षिप्तः श्वसनेन महात्मना।।5.1.126।।
339.e: "Angry Indra held the thunderbolt and came towards me chasing. At that time the great Wind-god tossed me into the air and dropped me down at once.

339.sa: अस्मिन्लवणतोये च प्रक्षिप्तः प्लवगोत्तम। गुप्तपक्षसमग्रश्च तव पित्राभिरक्षितः।।5.1.127।।
339.e: "O distinguished vanara your father, the Windgod threw me down into this saltwater sea. Thus my wings were protected.

339.sa: ततोऽहं मानयामि त्वां मान्यो हि मम मारुतः। त्वया मे ह्येष सम्बन्धः कपिमुख्य महागुणः।।5.1.128।।
339.e: "O esteemed vanara the Windgod is revered by me and so I honour you. O chief of monkeys, my bondage with you is therefore of high value to me, indeed.

339.sa: अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये सागरस्य ममैव च। प्रीतिं प्रीतमनाः कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि महाकपे।।5.1.129।।
339.e: "O great monkey when I hold you so high, you ought to oblige me and the (god of the) ocean wholeheartedly (and accept our hospitalty).

339.sa: श्रमं मोक्षय पूजां च गृहाण कपिसत्तम। प्रीतिं च बहुमन्यस्व प्रीतोऽस्मि तव दर्शनात्।।5.1.130।।
339.e: "O noble monkey oblige us by accepting our offering given with love and be relieved of your fatigue. Your presence itself is welcome to me".

339.sa: एवमुक्तः कपिश्रेष्ठस्तं नगोत्तममब्रवीत्। प्रीतोऽस्मि कृतमातिथ्यं मन्युरेषोऽपनीयताम्।।5.1.131।।
339.e: The great Hanuman, pleased with the words of Mainaka, said "I am pleased at your hospitality. Remove your unhappiness.

339.sa: त्वरते कार्यकालो मे अहश्चाप्यतिवर्तते। प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता न स्थातव्यमिहान्तरे।।5.1.132।।
339.e: "My commitment is hastening me. The day set (for the accomplishment of the task) is also drawing to a close. A vow is made and I will not halt in the middle of my work."

339.sa: इत्युक्त्वा पाणिना शैलमालभ्य हरिपुङ्गवः। जगामाकाशमाविश्य वीर्यवान् प्रहसन्निव।।5.1.133।।
339.e: Having said this, the mighty monkey gently touched the mountain with his hands before ascending to the sky with a smile on his face.

339.sa: स पर्वतसमुद्राभ्यां बहुमानादवेक्षितः। पूजितश्चोपपन्नाभिराशीर्भिरनिलात्मजः।।5.1.134।।
339.e: The mountain and the sea honoured and adored the son of the Windgod and gave him appropriate  blessings.

339.sa: अथोर्ध्वं दूरमुत्प्लुत्य हित्वा शैलमहार्णवौ। पितुः पन्थानमास्थाय जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे।।5.1.135।।
339.e: And thereafter leaping a long distance into the clear sky, he (Hanuman) took the path of the Windgod, his father, leaving behind the mountain and the sea.

339.sa: भूयश्चोर्ध्वं गतिं प्राप्य गिरिं तमवलोकयन्। वायुसूनुर्निरालम्बे जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे।।5.1.136।।
339.e: Rising higher and further up and looking at the mountain (which was going down into the ocean), the son of the Windgod coursed through the cloudless sky unsupported.

339.sa: तद् द्वितीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। प्रशशंसुः सुराः सर्वे सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः।।5.1.137।।
339.e: Gods, siddhas as well as the great sages praised him for the second great achievment of Hanuman, which is impossible for others to accomplish.

339.sa: देवताश्चाभवन् हृष्टास्तत्रस्थास्तस्य कर्मणा। काञ्चनस्य सुनाभस्य सहस्राक्षश्च वासवः।।5.1.138।।
339.e: The gods who happened to be present at that time (on the mountain) and the thousandeyed Indra were delighted by the gesture of golden Sunabha (Mainaka) mountain.

339.sa: उवाच वचनं धीमान् परितोषात्सगद्गदम्। सुनाभं पर्वतश्रेष्ठं स्वयमेव शचीपतिः।।5.1.139।।
339.e: Indra, the lord of Sachi, was personally satisfied and spoke to Mainaka, the best of mountains, in faltering tone, his throat choked out of joy.

339.sa: हिरण्यनाभ शैलेन्द्र परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते भृशम्। अभयं ते प्रयच्छामि तिष्ठ सौम्य यथासुखम्।।5.1.140।।
339.e: "O Hiranyanabha, the foremost among the mountains I am highly pleased with you. I give you security (free from fear of losing wings). O pious one you may stay on happily as you please.

339.sa: साह्यं कृतं ते सुमहद्विक्रान्तस्य हनूमतः। क्रमतो योजनशतं निर्भयस्य भये सति।।5.1.141।।
339.e: "You have rendered very valuable help to Hanuman who was attempting to leap  a distance of a hundred yojanas. He is fearless even when there is reason to fear (of falling down).

339.sa: रामस्यैष हितायैव याति दाशरथेर्हरिः। सत्क्रियां कुर्वता तस्य तोषितोऽस्मि दृढं त्वया।।5.1.142।।
339.e: "The vanara has gone on a mission to help the son of Dasaratha. I am highly pleased with the service rendered to him.

339.sa: ततः प्रहर्षमगमद्विपुलं पर्वतोत्तमः। देवतानां पतिं दृष्ट्वा परितुष्टं शतक्रतुम्।।5.1.143।।
339.e: Thereafter Mainaka, the great mountain was delighted to see Indra,  lord of the gods, performer of a hundred yajnas satisfied.

339.sa: स वै दत्तवरः शैलो बभूवावस्थितस्तदा। हनुमांश्च मुहूर्तेन व्यतिचक्राम सागरम्।।5.1.144।।
339.e: Then mount Mainaka, assured by Indra became secure. And Hanuman also crossed over the ocean in a short while.

339.sa: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। अब्रुवन् सूर्यसङ्काशां सुरसां नागमातरम्।।5.1.145।।
339.e: Then the gods, gandharvas, siddhas and great sages approached Surasa, the mother of nagas, who was glowing like the Sungod and said:.

339.sa: अयं वातात्मजः श्रीमान्प्लवते सागरोपरि। हनुमान्नाम तस्य त्वं मुहूर्तं विघ्नमाचर।।5.1.146।। राक्षसं रूपमास्थाय सुघोरं पर्वतोपमम्। दंष्ट्राकरालं पिङ्गाक्षं वक्त्रं कृत्वा नभः समम्।।5.1.147।।
339.e: "The glorious son of the Windgod, called Hanuman, is crossing the ocean. Obstruct him for sometime by assuming the hideous form of a demon, gigantic as a mountain, fearful with yellowishbrown eyes, with big teeth and a wide mouth like the sky.

339.sa: अयं वातात्मजः श्रीमान्प्लवते सागरोपरि। हनुमान्नाम तस्य त्वं मुहूर्तं विघ्नमाचर।।5.1.146।। राक्षसं रूपमास्थाय सुघोरं पर्वतोपमम्। दंष्ट्राकरालं पिङ्गाक्षं वक्त्रं कृत्वा नभः समम्।।5.1.147।।
339.e: "The glorious son of the Windgod, called Hanuman, is crossing the ocean. Obstruct him for sometime by assuming the hideous form of a demon, gigantic as a mountain, fearful with yellowishbrown eyes, with big teeth and a wide mouth like the sky.

339.sa: बलमिच्छामहे ज्ञातुं भूयश्चास्य पराक्रमम्। त्वां विजेष्यत्युपायेन विषादं वा गमिष्यति।।5.1.148।।
339.e: "We want to assess his strength, valour and intelligence once again. We wish to know whether he will win or give way to despondency".

339.sa: एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी दैवतैरभिसत्कृता। समुद्रमध्ये सुरसा बिभ्रती राक्षसं वपुः।।5.1.149।। विकृतं च विरूपं च सर्वस्य च भयावहम्। प्लवमानं हनूमन्तमावृत्येदमुवाच ह।।5.1.150।।
339.e: Thus honoured by the gods, Surasa assumed a terrific ugly form frightening to all and stood in the midst of the ocean. Putting up a distorted appearance and encompassing Hanuman who was crossing the ocean, she spoke to him:

339.sa: एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी दैवतैरभिसत्कृता। समुद्रमध्ये सुरसा बिभ्रती राक्षसं वपुः।।5.1.149।। विकृतं च विरूपं च सर्वस्य च भयावहम्। प्लवमानं हनूमन्तमावृत्येदमुवाच ह।।5.1.150।।
339.e: Thus honoured by the gods, Surasa assumed a terrific ugly form frightening to all and stood in the midst of the ocean. Putting up a distorted appearance and encompassing Hanuman who was crossing the ocean, she spoke to him:

339.sa: मम भक्षः प्रदिष्टस्त्वमीश्वरैर्वानरर्षभ। अहं त्वां भक्षयिष्यामि प्रविशेदं ममाननम्।।5.1.151।।
339.e: "O bull among vanaras the lords of the universe have provided you as food for me. I will eat you. Enter my mouth".

339.sa: एवमुक्तः सुरसया प्राञ्जलिर्वानरर्षभः। प्रहृष्टवदनः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।5.1.152।।
339.e: Thus addressed by Surasa,  the glorious Hanuman said this with a blooming face and folded hands:

339.sa: रामो दाशरथिर्नाम प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या चापि भार्यया।।5.1.153।।
339.e: "Dasaratha's son called Rama accompanied by his brother Lakshmana and his wife Vaidehi entered Dandaka forest.

339.sa: अन्यकार्यविषक्तस्य बद्धवैरस्य राक्षसैः। तस्य सीता हृता भार्या रावणेन यशस्विनी।।5.1.154।।
339.e: "While Rama was engaged otherwise, his glorious wife Sita was abducted by Ravana actuated by deeprooted enmity of demons with him.

339.sa: तस्याः सकाशं दूतोऽहं गमिष्ये रामशासनात्। कर्तुमर्हसि रामस्य साह्यं विषयवासिनि।।5.1.155।।
339.e: "I am going as Rama's emissary to search for his wife. It is proper for you to render help since you are a resident of his kingdom.

339.sa: अथवा मैथिलीं दृष्ट्वा रामं चाक्लिष्टकारिणम्। आगमिष्यामि ते वक्त्रं सत्यं प्रतिशृणोमि ते।।5.1.156।।
एवमुक्ता हनुमता सुरसा कामरूपिणी। अब्रवीन्नातिवर्तेन्मां कश्चिदेष वरो मम।।5.1.157।।
339.e: Having heard Hanuman, Surasa capable of taking any form at her free will told him that no one can cross (her region) as she had been given such a boon(by the Creator)৷৷

339.sa: तं प्रयान्तं समुद्वीक्ष्य सुरसा वाक्यमब्रवीत्। बलं जिज्ञासमाना वै नागमाता हनूमतः।।5.1.158।।
339.e: Surasa, mother of serpents, observing that Hanuman was attempting to escape, said this in order to gauge his strength:

339.sa: प्रविश्य वदनं मेऽद्य गन्तव्यं वानरोत्तम। वर एष पुरा दत्तो मम धात्रेति सत्वरा।।5.1.159।। व्यादाय विपुलं वक्त्रं स्थिता सा मारुतेः पुरः।
339.e: "O best vanara you must pass through my mouth today. Such is the boon granted to me by Brahma in the past". Then she quickly opened her big mouth and stood.

339.sa: एवमुक्तः सुरसया क्रुद्धो वानरपुङ्गवः।।5.1.160।। अब्रवीत्कुरु वै वक्त्रं येन मां विषहिष्यसे।
339.e: Thus addressed by Surasa, Hanuman the supreme vanara said, "Open your mouth wide enough to hold me."

339.sa: इत्युक्त्वा सुरसां क्रुद्धो धशयोजनमायता।।5.1.161।। दशयोजनविस्तारो बभूव हनुमांस्तदा।
339.e: Provoked by the words of Surasa, Hanuman stretched himself to ten yojanas.

339.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा मेघसङ्काशं दशयोजनमायतम्।।5.1.162।। चकार सुरसा चास्यं विंशद्योजनमायतम्।
339.e: Seeing his body stretched to ten yojanas like a cloud, Surasa also widened her mouth to twenty yojanas.

339.sa: हनुमांस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्त्रिंशद्योजनमायतः।।5.1.163।। चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं चत्वारिंशत्तथोच्छ्रितम्। बभूव हनुमावनीरः पञ्चाशद्योजनोच्छ्रितः।।5.1.164।।
339.e: Provoked, Hanuman further stretched his body to thirty yojanas and Surasa on her own enlarged her mouth to forty yojanas. Then the great hero Hanuman stretched his body to fifty yojanas.

339.sa: हनुमांस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्त्रिंशद्योजनमायतः।।5.1.163।। चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं चत्वारिंशत्तथोच्छ्रितम्। बभूव हनुमावनीरः पञ्चाशद्योजनोच्छ्रितः।।5.1.164।।
339.e: Provoked, Hanuman further stretched his body to thirty yojanas and Surasa on her own enlarged her mouth to forty yojanas. Then the great hero Hanuman stretched his body to fifty yojanas.

339.sa: चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं षष्टियोजनमायतम्। तथैव हनुमावनीरः सप्ततीयोजनोच्छ्रितः।।5.1.165।।
339.e: Surasa widened her mouth sixty yojanas and then the heroic Hanuman enlarged himself to seventy yojanas.

339.sa: चकार सुरसा वक्त्रमशीतीयोजनायतम्। हनुमानचलप्रख्यो नवतीयोजनोच्छ्रितः।।5.1.166।।
339.e: Surasa widened her mouth to eighy yojanas and the heroic Hanuman grew up to ninety yojanas, looking like a mountain.

339.sa: चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं शतयोजनमायतम् तव सानुषु विश्रान्तः शेषं प्रक्रमतामिति। तद्दृष्ट्वा व्यादितं त्वास्यं वायुपुत्रः सुबुद्धिमान्। दीर्घजिह्वं सुरसया सुघोरं नरकोपमम्।।5.1.167।। सुसंक्षिप्यात्मनः कायं बभूवाङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः।
339.e: Intelligent Hanuman observing Surasa's enlarged mouth open and dreadful like hell with a long tongue, suddenly shrunk his body to the size of a thumb.

339.sa: सोऽभिपत्याशु तद्वक्त्रं निष्पत्य च महाबलः। अन्तरिक्षे स्थितः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।5.1.168।।
339.e: Glorious and mighty  Hanuman quickly went into her mouth and got out and stood in the sky and said:.

339.sa: प्रविष्टोऽस्मि हि ते वक्त्रं दाक्षायणि नमोऽस्तु ते। गमिष्ये यत्र वैदेही सत्यं चासीद्वरस्तव।।5.1.169।।
339.e: "O Dakshayani I have indeed entered your mouth and your boon has come true (as nobody can go against the boon of the Creator). Allow me to proceed in quest of Vaidhehi. My salutations to you."

339.sa: तं दृष्ट्वा वदनान्मुक्तं चन्द्रं राहुमुखादिव। अब्रवीत्सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण वानरम्।।5.1.170।।
339.e: Seeing Hanuman released out of her mouth like the Moon released from the mouth of Rahu, Surasa assumed her true form and said:

339.sa: अर्थसिद्ध्यै हरिश्रेष्ठ गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम्। समानयस्व वैदेहीं राघवेण महात्मना।।5.1.171।।
339.e: "O noble vanara proceed happily to achieve your purpose. Go and unite Vaidehi with the noble self, Raghava.

339.sa: तत्तृतीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। साधु साध्विति भूतानि प्रशशंसुस्तदा हरिम्।।5.1.172।।
339.e: Witnessing Hanuman achieving a very difficult feat for the third time, all the living beings applauded him saying "Well done, welldone".

339.sa: स सागरमनाधृष्यमभ्येत्य वरुणालयम्। जगामाकाशमाविश्य वेगेन गरुडोपमः।।5.1.173।।
339.e: Rising above the invincible ocean, the abode of lord Varuna, Hanuman coursed through the sky speedily like Garuda.

339.sa: सेविते वारिधाराभिः पतगैश्च निषेविते। चरिते कैशिकाचार्यैरैरावतनिषेविते।।5.1.174।। सिंहकुञ्जरशार्दूलपतगोरगवाहनैः। विमानैः सम्पतद्भिश्च विमलैः समलङ्कृते।।5.1.175।। वज्राशनिसमाघातैः पावकैरुपशोभिते। कृतपुण्यैर्महाभागैः स्वर्गजिद्भिरलङ्कृते।।5.1.176।। वहता हव्यमत्यर्धं सेविते चित्रभानुना। ग्रहनक्षत्रचन्द्रार्कतारागण विभूषिते।।5.1.177।। महर्षिगणगन्धर्वनागयक्षसमाकुले। विविक्ते विमले विश्वे विश्वावसुनिषेविते।।5.1.178।। देवराजगजाक्रान्ते चन्द्रसूर्यपथे शिवे। विताने जीवलोकस्य वितते ब्रह्मनिर्मिते।।5.1.179।। बहुशः सेविते वीरैर्विद्याधरगणैर्वरैः। जगाम वायुमार्गे तु गरुत्मानिव मारुतिः।।5.1.180।।
339.e: Hanuman passed through the path of wind like Garuda. The region was refreshed with clouds that released torrents of rain and frequented by birds. The great masters of music (Tumburu, Narada and Gandharvas) trained in Kasika moved there driven by lions, elephants, tigers, birds and serpents and were moving in different aerial vehicles. It was splendid with god at fire who strikes fiercely like thunderbolt. It was inhabited by great sages who had acquired merit. The region was traversed by firegod who carried havis in large quantities earnestly. It was decorated with planets, constellations, Moon, Sun and clusters of stars. It was filled with groups of greal sages, gandharvas, nagas and yakshas. It was isolated part of the universe traversed by the king of gandharvas like Vishvavasu. It was an auspicious path for Moon and Sun, a sporting ground for Airavata, the vehicle of lord Indra. It was an extensive world of living beings created by Brahma. It was frequented by many heroes ascending to heaven and blocked by vidyadharas.
