344.sa: सहस्रं वाहिनीस्तत्र जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृताः।।5.6.34।। हेमजालपरिच्छन्नास्तरुणादित्यसन्निभाः। ददर्श राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य निवेशने।।5.6.35।।
344.e: He saw in the palace of Ravana, the demon king, thousands of troops adorned with gold, fully protected with armour of gold shining like the morning Sun.

344.sa: शिबिका विविधाकाराः स कपिर्मारुतात्मजः। लतागृहाणि चित्राणि चित्रशालागृहाणि च।।5.6.36।। क्रीडागृहाणि चान्यानि दारुपर्वतकानपि। कामस्य गृहकं रम्यं दिवागृहकमेव च।।5.6.37।। ददर्श राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य निवेशने।
344.e: The son of the Windgod saw at the palace of Ravana, the lord of demons, colourful palanquins of several kinds, bowers, picture galleries, spots for sporting, hillocks (artificial) made of wood, apartments for romance, for pleasures and day time activities.

344.sa: शिबिका विविधाकाराः स कपिर्मारुतात्मजः। लतागृहाणि चित्राणि चित्रशालागृहाणि च।।5.6.36।। क्रीडागृहाणि चान्यानि दारुपर्वतकानपि। कामस्य गृहकं रम्यं दिवागृहकमेव च।।5.6.37।। ददर्श राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य निवेशने।
344.e: The son of the Windgod saw at the palace of Ravana, the lord of demons, colourful palanquins of several kinds, bowers, picture galleries, spots for sporting, hillocks (artificial) made of wood, apartments for romance, for pleasures and day time activities.

344.sa: स मन्दरगिरिप्रख्यं मयूरस्थानसङ्कुलम्।।5.6.38।। ध्वजयष्टिभिराकीर्णं ददर्श भवनोत्तमम्। अनेकरत्नसङ्कीर्णं निधिजालं समन्ततः।।5.6.39।। धीरनिष्ठितकर्मान्तं गृहं भूतपतेरिव।
344.e: Comparable to mount Mandara, it was crowded with peacocks, set with flag staffs fixed all over, magnificent mansions built by skilled craftsmen with great efforts, decked with gems of several kinds, rich with treasures comparable to Kailasa, the home of Siva, the Lord of all beings.

344.sa: स मन्दरगिरिप्रख्यं मयूरस्थानसङ्कुलम्।।5.6.38।। ध्वजयष्टिभिराकीर्णं ददर्श भवनोत्तमम्। अनेकरत्नसङ्कीर्णं निधिजालं समन्ततः।।5.6.39।। धीरनिष्ठितकर्मान्तं गृहं भूतपतेरिव।
344.e: Comparable to mount Mandara, it was crowded with peacocks, set with flag staffs fixed all over, magnificent mansions built by skilled craftsmen with great efforts, decked with gems of several kinds, rich with treasures comparable to Kailasa, the home of Siva, the Lord of all beings.

344.sa: अर्चिर्भिश्चापि रत्नानां तेजसा रावणस्य च।।5.6.40।। विरराजाथ तद्वेश्म रश्मिमानिव रश्मिभिः।
344.e: The palace of Ravana looked splendid with gems of different hues and with Ravana's presence, it was shining like the radiant Sungod.

344.sa: जाम्बूनदमयान्येन शयनान्यासनानि च।।5.6.41।। भाजनानि च मुख्यानि ददर्श हरियूथपः।
344.e: The leader of the vanaras saw there beds, seats and main vessels made of gold.

344.sa: मध्वासवकृतक्लेदं मणिभाजनसङ्कुलम्।।5.6.42।। मनोरममसंबाधं कुबेरभवनं यथा। नूपुराणां च घोषेण काञ्चीनां निनदेन च।।5.6.43।। मृदङ्तलघोषैश्च घोषवद्भिर्विनादितम्। प्रासादसङ्घातयुतं स्त्रीरत्नशतसङ्कुलम्।।5.6.44। सुव्यूढकक्ष्यं हनुमान् प्रविवेश महागृहाम्।
344.e: Hanuman entered the delightful, lofty palace comparable to Kubera's mansion. It was filled with vessels encrusted with gems scattered all over. The floor was drenched with liquor. It was resonating with sounds of golden anklets of women and of drums. The rows of mansions, lofty palaces with welllaid apartments were full of hundreds of exquisite women. इत्यार्षे वाल्मीकीये श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे षष्ठस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

345.sa: स वेश्मजालं बलवान् ददर्श व्यासक्तवैडूर्यसुवर्णजालम्। यथा महत् प्रावृषि मेघजालं विद्युत्पिनद्धं सविहङ्गजालम्।।5.7.1।।
345.e: Powerful Hanuman beheld the conglomeration of buildings with golden lattices encrusted with vaidurya, with flocks of birds comparable to a complex of clouds pierced by lightning during rainy season.

345.sa: निवेशनानां विविधाश्च शालाः प्रधानशङ्खायुधचापशालाः। मनोहराश्चापि पुनर्विशालाः ददर्श वेश्माद्रिषु चन्द्रशालाः।।5.7.2।।
345.e: Attached to the spacious halls of the houses, were storehouses for valuable  conches, weapons, bows and arrows. On the top of the attics on these mansions, were large and delightful terraces open to the Moon.

345.sa: गृहाणि नानावसुराजितानि देवासुरैश्चापि सुपूजितानि। सर्वैश्च दोषैः परिवर्जितानि कपिर्ददर्श स्वबलार्जितानि।।5.7.3।।
345.e: The monkey saw numerous kinds of treasures, cherished by gods and demons, which were won by Ravana's might.

345.sa: तानि प्रयत्नाभिसमाहितानि मयेन साक्षादिव निर्मितानि। महीतले सर्वगुणोत्तराणि ददर्श लङ्काधिपतेर्गृहाणि।।5.7.4।।
345.e: The mansions of the lord of Lanka built with great care and  effort on earth were  by all means excellent  and appeared as though built personally by Maya (the divine architect wellknown for magical skills).

345.sa: ततो ददर्शोछ्रचितमेघरूपं मनोहरं काञ्चनचारुरूपम्। रक्षोऽधिपस्यात्मबलानुरूपं गृहोत्तमं ह्यप्रतिरूपरूपम्।।5.7.5।।
345.e: Hanuman beheld the magnificent and soulcaptivating palace possessing the splendour of molten gold. Of matchless beauty, it looked like a towering cloud worthy of the might of Ravana, the lord of ogresses.

345.sa: महीतले स्वर्गमिव प्रकीर्णं श्रिया ज्वलन्तं बहुरत्नकीर्णम्। नानातरूणां कुसुमावकीर्णं गिरेरिवाग्रं रजसावकीर्णम्।।5.7.6।।
345.e: It appeared splendid like a scattered piece of heaven on earth, glittering with countless gems. It looked like a mountain peak covered with pollen of flowers dropped from all kinds of trees.

345.sa: नारीप्रवेकैरिव दीप्यमानं तटिद्भिरम्भोदवदर्च्यमानम्। हंसप्रवेकैरिव वाह्यमानं श्रिया युतं खे सुकृतां विमानम्।।5.7.7।।
345.e: The aerial chariot was lit up by resplendent women just as a raincloud dazzles with flashes of lightning. It was auspicious, worthy of worship. It looked as if it was drawn by royal swans in the sky.

345.sa: यथा नगाग्रं बहुधातुचित्रं यथा नभश्च ग्रहचन्द्रचित्रम्। ददर्शयुक्तीकृतमेघचित्रं विमानरत्नं बहुरत्नचित्रम्।।5.7.8।।
345.e: A jewel among aerial chariots, it looked colourful with many gems beset. It appeared like the summit of a mountain decorated with the colours of minerals, like the sky bespangled with planets and the Moon and like a mass of multicoloured clouds adorned by a rainbow.

345.sa: मही कृता पर्वतराजिपूर्णा शैलाः कृता वृक्षवितानपूर्णाः। वृक्षाः कृताः पुष्पवितानपूर्णाः पुष्पं कृतं केसरपत्रपूर्णम्।।5.7.9।।
345.e: The whole  earth had been picturised on it. It was filled with rows of mountains  and a canopy of trees all over. The trees were filled with lovely flowers with petals and filaments drawn on them.

345.sa: कृतानि वेश्मानि च पाण्डुराणि तथा सुपुष्पाण्यपि पुष्कराणि। पुनश्च पद्मानि सकेसराणि धन्यानि चित्राणि तथा वनानि।।5.7.10।।
345.e: There were pictures of mansions white in colour and pools of crystalclear water filled with lovely flowers. There were pictures of beautiful lotuses drawn on it.

345.sa: पुष्पाह्वयं नामविराजमानं रत्नप्रभाभिश्च विवर्धमानम्। वेश्मोत्तमानामपि चोच्यमानं महाकपिस्तत्र महाविमानम्।।5.7.11।।
345.e: There, the great Hanuman indeed saw a splendid chariot called Pushpaka. It was glowing with glittering gems. Taller than the biggest mansion, it was a great chariot.

345.sa: कृताश्च वैडूर्यमया विहङ्गाः रूप्यप्रवालैश्च तथा विहङ्गाः। चित्राश्च नानावसुभिर्भुजङ्गाः जात्यानुरूपास्तुरगाः शुभाङ्गाः।।5.7.12।।
345.e: Inside were birds made of vaidurya, silver and corals. There were colourful serpents made of various gems, and highclass horses of exquisite limbs drawn.

345.sa: प्रवालजाम्बूनदपुष्पपक्षाः सलीलमावर्जितजिह्मपक्षाः। कामस्य साक्षादिव भान्ति पक्षाः कृता विहङ्गाः सुमुखाः सुपक्षाः।।5.7.13।।
345.e: It had curved figures of birds with beautiful wings carved out of corals and gold The wings were shining as if they were really the wings of allies of Cupid, the god of love.

345.sa: नियुज्यमानास्तु गजाः सुहस्ताः सकेसराश्चोत्पलपत्रहस्ताः। बभूवदेवी च कृता सुहस्ता लक्ष्मी स्तथा पद्मिनि पद्महस्ता।।5.7.14।।
345.e: He saw on it lotus ponds, artificial elephants with shapely trunks, offering to Laxmi who herself was a lotus, holding in her beautiful hands blue lotuses shining with filaments.

345.sa: इतीव तद्गृहमभिगम्य शोभनम् सविस्मयो नगमिव चारुशोभनम्। पुनश्च तत्परमसुगन्धि सुन्दरम् हिमात्यये नगमिव चारुकन्दरम्।।5.7.15।।
345.e: Thus he reached the auspicious palace appearing like a beautiful mountain and stood wonderstruck. Once again he looked at that beautiful palace which appeared like a mountain with lovely caverns in spring time filled with wonderful fragrance

345.sa: ततः स तां कपिरभिपत्य पूजितां चरन् पुरीं दशमुखबाहुपालिताम्। अदृश्य तां जनकसुतां सुपूजितां सुदुःखितः पतिगुणवेगवर्जिताम्।।5.7.16।।
345.e: Then Hanuman moved about that cherished city ruled by the strength of arms of the tenheaded king. Unable to find venerable Sita, who was deprived of the benefit of her husband's virtuous proximity, he became deeply sad.

345.sa: ततस्तदा बहुविधभावितात्मनः कृतात्मनो जनकसुतां सुवर्त्मनः। अपश्यतोऽभवदतिदुःखितं मनः सुचक्षुषः प्रविचरतो महात्मनः।।5.7.17।।
345.e: Unable to find Sita, the disciplined and foresighted Hanuman, who always kept the righteous path, felt distressed while moving about, his mind oppressed by all kinds of thought. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventh sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

346.sa: स तस्य मध्ये भवनस्य संस्थितं महद्विमानं मणिवज्रचित्रितम्। प्रतप्तजाम्बूनदजालकृत्रिमं ददर्श वीरः पवनात्मजः कपिः।।5.8.1।।
346.e: The courageous son of the Windgod, Hanuman, the vanara saw the aerial chariot kept in the middle of the mansion inlaid with gems and diamonds latticed with artificial windows of barnished gold.

346.sa: तदप्रमेयाप्रतिकारकृत्रिमं कृतं स्वयं साध्विति विश्वकर्मणा। दिवं गतं वायुपथप्रतिष्ठितं व्यराजतादित्यपथस्य लक्ष्मवत्।।5.8.2।।
346.e: The immeasurable Pushpaka fashioned by Visvakarma with images of incomparable beauty was not possible to describe. An excellent  product of his achievement, it was placed in the aerial path appearing as a beaconlight (signpost) in the orbit of the Sun.

346.sa: न तत्र किञ्चिन्न कृतं प्रयत्नतो न तत्र किञ्चिन्न महार्हरत्नवत्। न ते विशेषा नियताः सुरेष्वपि न तत्र किञ्चिन्न महाविशेषवत्।।5.8.3।।
346.e: There was nothing in Pushpaka which was not executed carefully with special effort, nothing which was not made of precious stones. Such privileges were not available to even gods. Indeed there was nothing which was not unique.

346.sa: तपः समाधानपराक्रमार्जितं मनः समाधानविचारचारिणम्। अनेकसंस्थानविशेषनिर्मितं ततस्ततस्तुल्यविशेषदर्शनम्।।5.8.4।।
346.e: (The Pushpaka) was designed by dint of divine efforts and prowess (of Kubera). It could touch any place its master commanded with a cool mind. It had many beautiful places of rest.

346.sa: विशेषमालम्ब्य विशेषसंस्थितं विचित्रकूटं बहुकूटमण्डितम्। मनोऽभिरामं शरदिन्दुनिर्मलं विचित्रकूटं शिखरं गिरेर्यथा।।5.8.5।।
346.e: The Pushpaka was specially designed in a unique manner. It was decorated with many colourful peaks. It was delghtful and pleasing to the mind and bright like the autumnal fullmoon. It looked like a mountain with many wonderful towers around.

346.sa: वहन्ति यं कुण्डलशोभिताननाः महाशना व्योमचरा निशाचराः। विवृत्तविध्वस्तविशाललोचनाः महाजवा भूतगणाः सहस्रशः।।5.8.6।।
346.e: The Pushpaka was borne by multitudes of Bhutas whose faces were shining with earrings, who were demons ranging in the night sky. They were gluttons endowed with great speed, and they had big, rolling and frightening eyes.

346.sa: वसन्तपुष्पोत्करचारुदर्शनं वसन्तमासादपि कान्तदर्शनम्। स पुष्पकं तत्र विमानमुत्तमं ददर्श तद्वानरवीरसत्तमः।।5.8.7।।
346.e: That hero among monkeys, beheld the aerial chariot looking beautiful like a colourful collection of spring blossoms. Its appearance was more pleasant than spring itself. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eighth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

347.sa: तस्यालयवरिष्ठस्य मध्ये विपुलमायतं। ददर्श भवनश्रेष्ठं हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः।।5.9.1।।
347.e: The son of the Windgod, Hanuman, saw a huge, spacious and excellent of all mansions in the centre of the palace.

347.sa: अर्धयोजनविस्तीर्णमायतं योजनं हि तत्। भवनं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य बहुप्रासादसङ्कुलम्।।5.9.2।।
347.e: The mansion of the lord of demons was a conglomeration of palaces half a yojana long and half a yojana wide.

347.sa: मार्गमाणस्तु वैदेहीं सीतामायतलोचनाम्। सर्वतः परिचक्राम हनूमानरिसूदनः।।5.9.3।।
347.e: Hanuman, the subduer of enemies, went  around in search of  the largeeyed Vaidehi.

347.sa: उत्तमं राक्षसावासं हनुमानवलोकयन्। आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्।।5.9.4।। चतुर्विषाणैर्द्विरदैस्त्रिविषाणैस्तथैव च। परिक्षिप्तमसम्बाधं रक्ष्यमाणमुदायुधैः।।5.9.5।।
347.e: Searching the excellent residences of important demons, Hanuman finally reached  the palace of the lord of ogres guarded by armed demons with elephants with two or three or four tusks.

347.sa: उत्तमं राक्षसावासं हनुमानवलोकयन्। आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्।।5.9.4।। चतुर्विषाणैर्द्विरदैस्त्रिविषाणैस्तथैव च। परिक्षिप्तमसम्बाधं रक्ष्यमाणमुदायुधैः।।5.9.5।।
347.e: Searching the excellent residences of important demons, Hanuman finally reached  the palace of the lord of ogres guarded by armed demons with elephants with two or three or four tusks.

347.sa: राक्षसीभिश्च पत्नीभी रावणस्य निवेशनम्। आहृताभिश्च विक्रम्य राजकन्याभिरावृतम्।।5.9.6।। तन्नक्रमकराकीर्णं तिमिङ्गिलझषाकुलम्। वायुवेगसमाधूतं पन्नगैरिव सागरम्।।5.9.7।।
347.e: Hanuman entered the palace of Ravana crowded with shedemons who were the wives of Ravana and the princesses brought by him after winning them in wars. To Hanuman, it looked like an ocean filled with crocodiles, sharks, whales, and a variety of fishes and snakes tossed by the force of the wind.

347.sa: राक्षसीभिश्च पत्नीभी रावणस्य निवेशनम्। आहृताभिश्च विक्रम्य राजकन्याभिरावृतम्।।5.9.6।। तन्नक्रमकराकीर्णं तिमिङ्गिलझषाकुलम्। वायुवेगसमाधूतं पन्नगैरिव सागरम्।।5.9.7।।
347.e: Hanuman entered the palace of Ravana crowded with shedemons who were the wives of Ravana and the princesses brought by him after winning them in wars. To Hanuman, it looked like an ocean filled with crocodiles, sharks, whales, and a variety of fishes and snakes tossed by the force of the wind.

347.sa: या हि वैश्रवणे लक्ष्मीर्या चेन्द्रे हरिवाहने। सा रावणगृहे सर्वा नित्यमेवानपायिनी।।5.9.8।।
347.e: Whatever wealth was possessed by Vaisravana (Kubera, the son of sage Vishrava) and also Indra who rides the Ucchaisrava green horse, was there in the palace of Ravana.

347.sa: या च राज्ञः कुबेरस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च। तादृशी तद्विशिष्टा वा ऋद्धी रक्षोगृहेष्विह।।5.9.9।।
347.e: The wealth stored in Ravana's palace was akin to what lay in the palaces of Kubera, Yama or Varuna, and ever more exquisite.

347.sa: तस्य हर्म्यस्य मध्यस्थं वेश्म चान्यत्सुनिर्मितं। बहुनिर्यूहसङ्कीर्णं ददर्श पवनात्मजः।।5.9.10।।
347.e: Hanuman saw in the centre of that palace a complex of many wellbuilt houses.

347.sa: ब्रह्मणोऽर्थे कृतं दिव्यं दिवि यद्विश्वकर्मणा। विमानं पुष्पकं नाम सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्।।5.9.11।। परेण तपसा लेभे यत्कुबेरः पितामहात्। कुबेरमोजसा जित्वा लेभे तद्राक्षसेश्वरः।।5.9.12।।
347.e: There was a wonderful aerial chariot called Pushpaka embellished with all kinds of gems built by Visvakarma for Brahma. It was the same one that Kubera had won from his grandfather, the creator Brahma, through his supreme penance. The lord of ogres acquired it (as a memento for his victory) by defeating Kubera with his might.

347.sa: ब्रह्मणोऽर्थे कृतं दिव्यं दिवि यद्विश्वकर्मणा। विमानं पुष्पकं नाम सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्।।5.9.11।। परेण तपसा लेभे यत्कुबेरः पितामहात्। कुबेरमोजसा जित्वा लेभे तद्राक्षसेश्वरः।।5.9.12।।
347.e: There was a wonderful aerial chariot called Pushpaka embellished with all kinds of gems built by Visvakarma for Brahma. It was the same one that Kubera had won from his grandfather, the creator Brahma, through his supreme penance. The lord of ogres acquired it (as a memento for his victory) by defeating Kubera with his might.

347.sa: ईहामृगसमायुक्त्तै: कार्तस्वरहिरमण्मयैः। सुकृतैराचितं स्तम्भैः प्रदीप्तमिव च श्रिया।।5.9.13।। मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशैरुल्लिखद्भिरिवाम्बरं। कूटागारैश्शुभाकारैस्सर्वतस्समलङ्कृतम्।।5.9.14।।
347.e: It was supported by finely built pillars of two types of gold (Kartaswara and Hiranmaya) with images of wolves carved on them and blazing. It was tall as if scraping the sky and resembled mountains like Meru and Mandara. It was graced with multitudes of  auspicious and decorated pleasurehouses everywhere.

347.sa: ईहामृगसमायुक्त्तै: कार्तस्वरहिरमण्मयैः। सुकृतैराचितं स्तम्भैः प्रदीप्तमिव च श्रिया।।5.9.13।। मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशैरुल्लिखद्भिरिवाम्बरं। कूटागारैश्शुभाकारैस्सर्वतस्समलङ्कृतम्।।5.9.14।।
347.e: It was supported by finely built pillars of two types of gold (Kartaswara and Hiranmaya) with images of wolves carved on them and blazing. It was tall as if scraping the sky and resembled mountains like Meru and Mandara. It was graced with multitudes of  auspicious and decorated pleasurehouses everywhere.

347.sa: ज्वलनार्कप्रतीकाशं सुकृतं विश्वकर्मणा। हेमसोपानसंयुक्तं चारुप्रवरवेदिकम्।।5.9.15।।
347.e: It was well built by Visvakarma and and had golden stairways, with radiant platforms glowing like fire and Sun.

347.sa: जालवातायनैर्युक्तं काञ्चनैः स्स्फाटिकैरपि। इन्द्रनीलमहानीलमणिप्रवरवेदिकम्।।5.9.16।।
347.e: It had latticed windows made of gold inlaid with crystals. The platforms were encrusted with saphires called Indraneela and Mahaneela appropriately.

347.sa: विद्रुमेण विचित्रेण मणिभिश्च महाघनैः। निस्तुलाभिश्च मुक्ताभिस्तलेनाभिविराजितम्।।5.9.17।।
347.e: It was shining bright with colourful corals, precious gems and peerless pearls fixed on its floor.

347.sa: चन्दनेन च रक्तेन तपनीयनिभेन च। सुपुण्यगन्धिना युक्तमादित्यतरुणोपमम्।।5.9.18।।
347.e: It was bright like molten gold, fragrant with red sandal comparable to the rising Sun.

347.sa: कूटागारैर्वराकारैर्विविधैस्समलङ्कृतम्। विमानं पुष्पकं दिव्यमारुरोह महाकपिः।।5.9.19।।
347.e: Hanuman ascended the wonderful Pushpaka, welldecked with many corridors.

347.sa: तत्रस्थस्स तदा गन्धं पानभक्ष्यान्नसम्भवम्। दिव्यं सम्मूर्छितं जिघ्रद्रूपवन्तमिवानिलम्।।5.9.20।।
347.e: There he smelt the stupefying, unearthly odour of food and drink. He felt as though the fragrance had taken a potentially solid form. (Note: The wind has no form. But when he carried the aroma of food and drink it appeared like the personification of wind which could be smelt. गन्धवती पृथवी fragrance comes from earth पृथवीतत्त्व the poet transmits the same to the wind who has got only स्पर्श sense of touch).

347.sa: स गन्धस्तं महासत्त्वं बन्धुर्बन्धुमिवोत्तमम्। इत एहीत्युवाचेन तत्र यत्र स रावणः।।5.9.21।।
347.e: The fragrance was as if inviting the mighty hero like a relative inviting his kith and kin, saying 'come here' and leading him to a place where Ravana rested.

347.sa: ततस्तां प्रस्थितश्शालां ददर्श महतीं शुभाम्। रावणस्य मनः कान्तां कान्तामिव वरस्त्रियम्।।5.9.22।।
347.e: Then he proceeded to an auspicious hall, which was Ravana's favourite like his chief queen dear to his heart.

347.sa: मणिसोपानविकृतां हेमजालविभूषिताम्। स्फाटिकैरावृततलां दन्तान्तरितरूपिकाम्।।5.9.23।।
347.e: The stairways of the mansion were inlaid with special gems, windows were latticed with gold, floors were covered with crystals, figures of ivory with silver.

347.sa: मुक्ताभिश्च प्रवालैश्च रूप्यचामीकरैरपि। विभूषितां मणिस्तम्भैस्सुबहुस्तम्भभूषिताम्।।5.9.24।।
347.e: It was decorated with pillars of silver and gold inlaid with pearls and corals and gems.

347.sa: नम्रैरृजुभिरत्युच्चैस्समन्तात्सुविभूषितैः। स्तम्भै: पक्षैरिवात्युच्चैर्दिवं संप्रस्थितामिव।।5.9.25।।
347.e: It had highly ornamented pillars all over, some slightly bent and others straight. With lofty columns looking like wings it appeared as if the mansion had started on its journey to heaven.

347.sa: महत्या कुथयास्तीर्णां पृथिवीलक्षणाङ्कया। पृथिवीमिव विस्तीर्णां सराष्ट्रगृहमालिनीम्।।5.9.26।।
347.e: The floor was covered with a wide carpet spread from wall to wall with designs of different murals of many places and houses drawn in a row (garland like). The big carpet appeared like the expanse of earth itself.

347.sa: नादितां मत्तविहगैर्दिव्यगन्धाधिवासिताम्। परार्ध्यास्तरणोपेतां रक्षोधिपनिषेविताम्।।5.9.27।।
347.e: The mansion was resounding with the noise of birds singing in heat. It had wonderful fragrance. It was laid with exquisite tapestries and served as a dwelling place for the king of demons.

347.sa: धूम्रामगरुधूपेन विमलां हंसपाण्डुराम्। चित्रां पुष्पोपहारेण कल्माषीमिव सुप्रभाम्।।5.9.28।।
347.e: It was smoky with fumes of agaru incence though spotless like a swan. It was colourful and radiant like Kamadhenu, the wishfulfilling cow, because of the offering of flowers.

347.sa: मनस्संह्लादजननीं वर्णस्यापि प्रसादिनीम्। तां शोकनाशिनीं दिव्यां श्रियः सञ्जननीमिव।।5.9.29।।
347.e: (The mansion) was so full of effulgence and soul ravishing that it served as an adornment even to splendour. It looked as though it banished all sorrow and was a source of prosperity.

347.sa: इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थैस्तु पञ्च पञ्चभिरुत्तमैः। तर्पयामास मातेव तदा रावणपालिता।।5.9.30।।
347.e: The chamber of Ravana, like a mother, gratified all the five senses of Hanuman with proper objects of the senses.

347.sa: स्वर्गोऽयं देवलोकोऽयमिन्द्रस्येयं पुरी भवेत्। सिद्धिर्वेयं परा हि स्यादित्यमन्यत मारुतिः।।5.9.31।।
347.e: 'This may be heaven or world of gods. It may be Amaravati, the abode of Indra or else it may be the supreme achievment (of the Creator), thought Maruti৷৷

347.sa: प्रध्यायत इवापश्यत्प्रदीपांस्तत्र काञ्चनान्। धूर्तानिव महाधूतैर्देवनेन पराजितान्।।5.9.32।।
347.e: Seeing the golden lamps that stood burning steadily, Hanuman thought they looked like  gamblers in deep thought defeated by expert  gamblers in a game of dice.

347.sa: दीपानां च प्रकाशेन तेजसा रावणस्य च। अर्चिर्भिर्भूषणानां च प्रदीप्तेत्यभ्यमन्यत।।5.9.33।।
347.e: Hanuman fancied that the entire place was set ablaze with the glow of lamps, the lustre of Ravana and the brilliant glow of Ravana's ornaments (everything was shining).

347.sa: ततोऽपश्यत्कुथाऽऽसीनं नानावरायम्बरस्रजम्। सहस्रं वरनारीणां नानावेषविभूषितम्।।5.9.34।।
347.e: He found thousands of beautiful women seated on carpets wearing different clothes and garlands and dressed in various attires.

347.sa: परिवृत्तेऽर्धरात्रे तु पाननिद्रावशं गतम्। क्रीडित्वोपरतं रात्रौ सुष्वाप बलवत्तदा।।5.9.35।।
347.e: Drinking and sporting until midnight, they had dropped off to sleeptired.

347.sa: तत्प्रसुप्तं विरुरुचे निश्शब्दान्तरभूषणम्। निःशब्दहंसभ्रमरं यथा पद्मवनं महत्।।5.9.36।।
347.e: Fast asleep, sounds of their ornaments silenced, the young women looked like a large bed of lotuses with swans and bees sitting calm without their usual noise.

347.sa: तासां संवृतदन्तानि मीलिताक्षीणि मारुतिः। अपश्यत्पद्मगन्धीनि वदनानि सुयोषिताम्।।5.9.37।।
347.e: Hanuman looked at the faces of the wellbred young women with closed eyes and concealed teeth, fragrant like lotuses.

347.sa: प्रबुद्धानीव पद्मानि तासां भूत्वा क्षपाक्षये। पुनस्संवृतपत्राणि रात्राविव बभुस्तदा।।5.9.38।।
347.e: The faces of the women looked like blooming lotuses at daybreak, their petals closed up again at night.

347.sa: इमानि मुखपद्मानि नियतं मत्तषट्पदाः। अम्बुजानीव फुल्लानि प्रार्थयन्ति पुनः पुनः।।5.9.39।।
347.e: The intoxicated bees would again and again long to enjoy these beautiful faces which were like blooming lotuses.

347.sa: इति चामन्यत श्रीमानुपपत्त्या महाकपिः। मेने हि गुणतस्तानि समानि सलिलोद्भवैः।।5.9.40।।
347.e: The illustrious Hanuman felt it to be correct to compare those faces with lotuses for their fragrance.

347.sa: सा तस्य शुशुभे शाला ताभिस्त्रीभिर्विराजिता। शारदीव प्रसन्ना द्यौस्ताराभिरभिशोभिता।।5.9.41।।
347.e: Brightened by (the beauty of) the maidens, the mansion shone like the autumnal sky endearing  and pleasing with stars.

347.sa: स च ताभिः परिवृतश्शुशुभे राक्षसाधिपः। यथा ह्युडुपतिश्शीमांस्ताराभिरभिसंवृतः।।5.9.42।।
347.e: The lord of demons surrounded by women shone like the beautiful Moon encircled by stars.

347.sa: याश्च्यवन्तेऽम्बरात्ताराः पुण्यशेषसमावृताः। इमास्तास्सङ्गताः कृत्स्ना इति मेने हरिस्तदा।।5.9.43।।
347.e: Seeing those women lying together Hanuman imagined them to be numerous meteors dropped from heaven after enjoying their merits, enjoyed and exhausted.

347.sa: ताराणामिव सुव्यक्तं महतीनां शुभार्चिषाम्। प्रभावर्णप्रसादाश्च विरेजुस्तत्र योषिताम्।।5.9.44।।
347.e: It was clear that the grace and lustre of those women looked brilliant like the lustre and grace of brilliant stars releasing an auspicious glow.

347.sa: व्यावृत्तगुरुपीनस्रक्प्रकीर्णवरभूषणाः। पानव्यायामकालेषु निद्रापहृतचेतसः।।5.9.45।।
347.e: Garlands displaced and jewels scattered, they were drowsy due to drink and sexual exercise.

347.sa: व्यावृत्ततिलकाः काश्चित्काश्चिदुद्भ्रन्तनूपुराः। पार्श्वे गलितहाराश्च काश्चित्परमयोषितः।।5.9.46।।
347.e: A few young women had their circular vermilion mark (on the forehead) smudged, some had their anklets loosened and a few had their necklaces.

347.sa: मुक्ताहाराऽवृताश्चान्याः काश्चिद्विस्रस्तवाससः। व्याविद्धरशनादामाः किशोर्य इव वाहिताः।।5.9.47।।
347.e: Some had their strings of pearl broken, others had their clothes slipped off, and some had their waist belts snapped. They were like young mares fallen to rest after carrying heavy loads.

347.sa: सुकुण्डलधराश्चान्या विच्छिन्नमृदितस्रजः। गजेन्द्रमृदिताः फुल्ला लता इव महावने।।5.9.48।।
347.e: With their good eartops broken and flower garlands crushed some looked like blooming creepers in a dense forest crushed by mighty elephants.

347.sa: चन्द्रांशुकिरणाभाश्च हाराः कासांचिदुत्कटाः। हंसा इव बभुस्सुप्ताः स्तनमध्येषु योषिताम्।।5.9.49।।
347.e: The pearl chains, large and shining like rays of the Moon in the space between the breasts looked like sleeping swans.

347.sa: अपरासां च वैडूर्याः कादम्बा इव पक्षिणः। हेमसूत्राणि चान्यासां चक्रवाका इवाभवन्।।5.9.50।।
347.e: The vaidurya worn by women (on the breasts) looked like Kadamba birds while the golden chains put on by some others appeared like ruddy geese.

347.sa: हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः। आपगा इव ता रेजुर्जघनैः पुलिनैरिव।।5.9.51।।
347.e: Their hips were like river banks crowded with swans, karandava and Chakravaka birds shining like rivers.

347.sa: किङ्किणीजालसङ्कोशास्ता हैमविपुलाम्बुजाः। भावग्राहा यशस्तीराः सुप्ता नद्य इवाऽऽबभुः।।5.9.52।।
347.e: With their tiny bells round their girdle looking like buds, the bold golden ornaments like lotuses, their gestures of love like crocodiles and their radiant beauty like silver banks, the women looked like smoky rivers.

347.sa: मृदुष्वङ्गेषु कासाञ्चित्कुचाग्रेषु च संस्थिताः। बभुर्वर्भूषणानीव शुभा भूषणराजयः।।5.9.53।।
347.e: The beautiful imprints made by the (heavy) ornaments on the tender limbs, breasts and nipples of some women appeared like many ornaments.

347.sa: अंशुकान्ताश्च कासाञ्चिन्मुखमारुतकम्पिताः। उपर्युपरि वक्त्राणां व्याधूयन्ते पुनः पुनः।।5.9.54।।
347.e: Shaken by the breath released from their mouths the fringes of the garments of some women were drawn towards their faces again and againfluttering.

347.sa: ताः पताका इवोद्धूताः पत्नीनां रुचिरप्रभाः। नानावर्णसुवर्णानां वक्त्रमूलेषु रेजिरे।।5.9.55।।
347.e: The fringes of their garments glowing beautifully close to the faces of the wives (of Ravana) with different beautiful hues, shone splendid like flags.

347.sa: ववल्गुश्चात्र कासांचित्कुण्डलानि शुभार्चिषाम्। मुखमारुतसंसर्गान्मन्दं मन्दं सुयोषिताम्।।5.9.56।।
347.e: The eartops of some women endowed with auspicious charm were swinging softly generating a gentle sound by the touch of their breath.

347.sa: शर्कराऽसवगन्धैश्च प्रकृत्या सुरभिः सुखः। तासां वदननिश्वासस्सिषेवे रावणं तदा।।5.9.57।।
347.e: The sweet smell of wine emitted from their mouth and the natural fragrance of their breath was refreshing to Ravana  as if it was serving him at that time.

347.sa: रावणाननशङ्काश्च काश्चिद्रावणयोषितः। मुखानि स्म सपत्नीनामुपाजिघ्रन्पुनः पुनः।।5.9.58।।
347.e: Some women of Ravana (overcome by blind passion) smelt again and again the mouths of their cowives next to them  assuming it to be Ravana's.

347.sa: अत्यर्थं सक्तमनसो रावणे ता वरस्त्रियः। अस्वतन्त्राः सपत्नीनां प्रियमेवाऽचरंस्तदा।।5.9.59।।
347.e: Even though the beautiful wives (should have been angry with their cowives for smelling their mouths) they behaved pleasingly, having no freedom to act with Ravana

347.sa: बाहूनुपनिधायान्याः पारिहार्यविभूषितान्। अंशुकानि च रम्याणि प्रमदास्तत्र शिश्यिरे।।5.9.60।।
347.e: Some women slept pillowed on their arms, laying aside their adornments and others had their garment under the head as pillows and lay in sleep.

347.sa: अन्या वक्षसि चान्यस्यास्तस्याः काचित्पुनर्भुजम्। अपरा त्वङ्कमन्यस्यास्तस्याश्चाप्यपरा भुजौ।।5.9.61।।
347.e: Some women lay placing their arms on the breasts of the other while their own arms were used as pillow by another. One woman placed her head  on the lap of the other and slept.

347.sa: ऊरुपार्श्वकटीपृष्ठमन्योन्यस्य समाश्रिताः। परस्परनिविष्टाङ्ग्यो मदस्नेहवशानुगाः।।5.9.62।।
347.e: Given to intoxication and sex, the women slept touching one another's thighs, sides, hips, back and lap of the other, with their limbs intertwined.

347.sa: अन्योन्यभुजसूत्रेण स्त्रीमाला ग्रथिता हि सा। मालेव ग्रथिता सूत्रे शुशुभे मत्तषट्पदा।।5.9.63।।
347.e: Knit with the shoulders of one another like a garland of flowers intertwined with the tipsy bees resting the women shone.

347.sa: लतानां माधवे मासि फुल्लानां वायुसेवनात्। अन्योन्य मालाग्रथितं संसक्तकुसुमोच्चयम्।।5.9.64।। व्यतिवेष्टितसुस्कन्धमन्योन्यभ्रमराकुलम्। आसीद्वनमिवोद्धूतं स्त्रीवनं रावणस्य तत्।।5.9.65।।
347.e: The women of Ravana appeared like a garden in spring. They were as if a cluster of creepers blossomed in spring due to the caresses of the breeze. They were knit together as one string forming a garland, flowers of one creeper striking the other. The joints of these creepers had grown strong when tangled together. Shaken by the breeze, the bees resting on one creeper would go to the other.

347.sa: लतानां माधवे मासि फुल्लानां वायुसेवनात्। अन्योन्य मालाग्रथितं संसक्तकुसुमोच्चयम्।।5.9.64।। व्यतिवेष्टितसुस्कन्धमन्योन्यभ्रमराकुलम्। आसीद्वनमिवोद्धूतं स्त्रीवनं रावणस्य तत्।।5.9.65।।
347.e: The women of Ravana appeared like a garden in spring. They were as if a cluster of creepers blossomed in spring due to the caresses of the breeze. They were knit together as one string forming a garland, flowers of one creeper striking the other. The joints of these creepers had grown strong when tangled together. Shaken by the breeze, the bees resting on one creeper would go to the other.

347.sa: उचितेष्वपि सुव्यक्तं न तासां योषितां तदा। विवेकः शक्य आधातुं भूषणाङ्गाम्बरस्रजाम्।।5.9.66।।
347.e: It was not possible to distinguish clearly between their jewels, limbs, garments and garlands and to place them in the right spots.

347.sa: रावणे सुखसंविष्टे तास्त्रियो विविधप्रभाः। ज्वलन्तः काञ्चना दीपाः प्रैक्षन्तानिमिषा इव।।5.9.67।।
347.e: When Ravana was happily asleep, the gods of light burning on the gold lampposts gazed without winking as it were, at the women, whom they dare  not gaze for fear of waking Ravana.

347.sa: राजर्षिपितृदैत्यानां गन्धर्वाणां च योषितः। राक्षसानां च याः कन्यास्तस्य कामवशं गताः।।5.9.68।।
347.e: The women halled from the families of royal sages, ancestral deities, daityas and demons who were infatuated with him.

347.sa: युद्धकामेन ताः सर्वा रावणेन हृताः स्त्रियः। समदा मदनेनैव मोहिताः काश्चिदागताः।।5.9.69।।
347.e: Many were brought by Ravana as captives of war and some came on their own deluded by lust.

347.sa: न तत्र काचित्प्रमदा प्रसह्य वीर्योपपन्नेन गुणेन लब्धा। न चान्यकामापि न चान्यपूर्वा विना वरार्हां जनकात्मजां ताम्।।5.9.70।।
347.e: Except Sita no other woman among them had been taken there by force. They were won only on account of his valour and virtues. None loved any one earlier and none was married to others.

347.sa: न चाकुलीना न च हीनरूपा नादक्षिणा नानुपचारयुक्ता। भार्याभवत्तस्य न हीनसत्त्वा न चापि कान्तस्य न कामनीया।।5.9.71।।
347.e: None among them was born of a lowly family, nor lacked beauty, kindness, skill, strength or brightness. No one was not lovable to Ravana.

347.sa: बभूव बुद्धिस्तु हरीश्वरस्य यदीदृशी राघवधर्मपत्नी। इमा यथा राक्षसराजभार्याः सुजातमस्येति हि साधुबुद्धेः।।5.9.72।।
347.e: 'If the lawful wife of Rama born of a good family can be allowed to remain with Rama in the same way as the consorts of the lord of demons, how fortunate it would be, thought the wise lord of monkeys'.

347.sa: पुनश्च सोऽचिन्तयादात्तरूपो ध्रुवं विशिष्टा गुणतो हि सीता। अथायमस्यां कृतवान्महात्मा लङ्केश्वरः कष्टमनार्यकर्म।।5.9.73।।
347.e: Hanuman once again assuming his true form said to himself, 'Sita is surely a virtuous lady superior to and more distinguished than them all. Alas, this lord of Lanka committed an ignoble, act (by abducting her). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे नवमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the ninth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

348.sa: तत्र दिव्योपमं मुख्यं स्फाटिकं रत्नभूषितम्। अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान् ददर्श शयनासनम्।।5.10.1।। दान्तकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैर्वैडूर्यैश्च वरासनैः। महार्हास्तरणोपेतैरुपपन्नं महाधनैः।।5.10.2।।
348.e: Looking around, Hanuman noticed a bed chamber, with a heavenly dais on which he saw a couch encrusted with crystals, vaidurya, and inlaid with colourful ivory and gold. It had an exquisite rich covering.

348.sa: तत्र दिव्योपमं मुख्यं स्फाटिकं रत्नभूषितम्। अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान् ददर्श शयनासनम्।।5.10.1।। दान्तकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैर्वैडूर्यैश्च वरासनैः। महार्हास्तरणोपेतैरुपपन्नं महाधनैः।।5.10.2।।
348.e: Looking around, Hanuman noticed a bed chamber, with a heavenly dais on which he saw a couch encrusted with crystals, vaidurya, and inlaid with colourful ivory and gold. It had an exquisite rich covering.

348.sa: तस्य चैकतमे देशे सोऽग्य्रमालाविभूषितम्। ददर्श पाण्डुरं छत्रं ताराधिपतिसन्निभम्।।5.10.3।।
348.e: Hanuman saw an umbrella in one spot decorated with the best of garlands. The white umbrella looked like the Moon, lord of stars.

348.sa: जातरूपपरिक्षिप्तं चित्रभानुसमप्रभम्। अशोकमालाविततं ददर्श परमासनम्।।5.10.4।। वालव्यजनहस्ताभिर्वीज्यमानं समन्ततः। गन्धैश्च विविधैर्जुष्टं वरधूपेन धूपितम्।।5.10.5।। परमास्तरणास्तीर्णमाविकाजिनसंवृतम्। दामभिर्वरमाल्यानां समन्तादुपशोभितम्।।5.10.6।।
348.e: He saw an exquisite couch made of gold shining wonderfully like the Sun. It was decorated with ashoka flowers. Women were holding fans of chamari deer. It was upholstered with the best of bedspreads made of soft sheep skin and adorned with beautiful strings of flower garlands. Scented with aromatic smoke, it was refreshed with fragrance which had spread all over the place.

348.sa: जातरूपपरिक्षिप्तं चित्रभानुसमप्रभम्। अशोकमालाविततं ददर्श परमासनम्।।5.10.4।। वालव्यजनहस्ताभिर्वीज्यमानं समन्ततः। गन्धैश्च विविधैर्जुष्टं वरधूपेन धूपितम्।।5.10.5।। परमास्तरणास्तीर्णमाविकाजिनसंवृतम्। दामभिर्वरमाल्यानां समन्तादुपशोभितम्।।5.10.6।।
348.e: He saw an exquisite couch made of gold shining wonderfully like the Sun. It was decorated with ashoka flowers. Women were holding fans of chamari deer. It was upholstered with the best of bedspreads made of soft sheep skin and adorned with beautiful strings of flower garlands. Scented with aromatic smoke, it was refreshed with fragrance which had spread all over the place.

348.sa: जातरूपपरिक्षिप्तं चित्रभानुसमप्रभम्। अशोकमालाविततं ददर्श परमासनम्।।5.10.4।। वालव्यजनहस्ताभिर्वीज्यमानं समन्ततः। गन्धैश्च विविधैर्जुष्टं वरधूपेन धूपितम्।।5.10.5।। परमास्तरणास्तीर्णमाविकाजिनसंवृतम्। दामभिर्वरमाल्यानां समन्तादुपशोभितम्।।5.10.6।।
348.e: He saw an exquisite couch made of gold shining wonderfully like the Sun. It was decorated with ashoka flowers. Women were holding fans of chamari deer. It was upholstered with the best of bedspreads made of soft sheep skin and adorned with beautiful strings of flower garlands. Scented with aromatic smoke, it was refreshed with fragrance which had spread all over the place.

348.sa: तस्मिन् जीमूतसंकाशं प्रदीप्तोत्तमकुण्डलम्। लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुं महारजतवाससम्।।5.10.7।। लोहितेनानुलिप्ताङ्गं चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना। सन्ध्यारक्तमिवाकाशे तोयदं सतटिद्गणम्।।5.10.8।। वृतमाभरणैर्दिव्यैः सुरूपं कामरूपिणम्। सवृक्षवनगुल्माढ्यं प्रसुप्तमिव मन्दरम्।।5.10.9।। क्रीडित्वोपरतं रात्रौ वराभरणभूषितम्। प्रियं राक्षसकन्यानां राक्षसानां सुखावहम्।।5.10.10।। पीत्वाऽप्युपरतं चापि ददर्श स महाकपिः। भास्वरे शयने वीरं प्रसुप्तं राक्षसाधिपम्।।5.10.11।।
348.e: Hanuman saw the mightyarmed, heroic lord of demons, sleeping with huge bloodshot eyes looking like a cloud, he was adorned with flashing earrings, and clad in robes of silver texture. His body was smeared with red sandal paste of sweet fragrance. Therefore, he looked like a cloud reddened by twilight and flashing with the lightning of his ornaments. He was handsome and could assume any form at will. He looked like Mandara mountain surrounded thickly with  trees and wild bushes. Decked with exquisite ornaments, he was sleeping after dalliance at night on that glittering couch. He was the beloved of the ogresses and bringer of joy to them

348.sa: तस्मिन् जीमूतसंकाशं प्रदीप्तोत्तमकुण्डलम्। लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुं महारजतवाससम्।।5.10.7।। लोहितेनानुलिप्ताङ्गं चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना। सन्ध्यारक्तमिवाकाशे तोयदं सतटिद्गणम्।।5.10.8।। वृतमाभरणैर्दिव्यैः सुरूपं कामरूपिणम्। सवृक्षवनगुल्माढ्यं प्रसुप्तमिव मन्दरम्।।5.10.9।। क्रीडित्वोपरतं रात्रौ वराभरणभूषितम्। प्रियं राक्षसकन्यानां राक्षसानां सुखावहम्।।5.10.10।। पीत्वाऽप्युपरतं चापि ददर्श स महाकपिः। भास्वरे शयने वीरं प्रसुप्तं राक्षसाधिपम्।।5.10.11।।
348.e: Hanuman saw the mightyarmed, heroic lord of demons, sleeping with huge bloodshot eyes looking like a cloud, he was adorned with flashing earrings, and clad in robes of silver texture. His body was smeared with red sandal paste of sweet fragrance. Therefore, he looked like a cloud reddened by twilight and flashing with the lightning of his ornaments. He was handsome and could assume any form at will. He looked like Mandara mountain surrounded thickly with  trees and wild bushes. Decked with exquisite ornaments, he was sleeping after dalliance at night on that glittering couch. He was the beloved of the ogresses and bringer of joy to them

348.sa: निःश्वसन्तं यथा नागं रावणं वानरर्षभः। आसाद्य परमोद्विग्नस्सोपासर्पत्सुभीतवत्।।5.10.12।।
348.e: Having reached Ravana, who was breathing (hissing) like a snake, Hanuman was for a moment frightened and drew away from him as if he was put to terrible fear.

348.sa: अथाऽऽरोहणमासाद्य वेदिकाऽन्तरमाश्रितः। सुप्तं राक्षसशार्दूलं प्रेक्षते स्म महाकपिः।।5.10.13।।
348.e: The great vanara ascended the stairway and reached another altar and once again looked at the sleeping Ravana, the tiger among demons.

348.sa: शुशुभे राक्षसेन्द्रस्य स्वपतः शयनोत्तमम्। गन्धहस्तिनि संविष्टे यथा प्रस्रवणं महत्।।5.10.14।।
348.e: While the lord of demons lay asleep on the magnificent couch, he  looked like the Prasravana hill with its elephant in rut.

348.sa: काञ्चनाङ्गदसन्नध्दै च ददर्श स महात्मनः। विक्षिप्तौ राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भुजाविन्द्रध्वजोपमौ।।5.10.15।। ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरापीडनकृतव्रणौ। वज्रोल्लिखितपीनांसौ विष्णुचक्रपरिक्षतौ।।5.10.16।। पीनौ समसुजातांसौ संगतौ बलसंयुतौ। सुलक्षणनखाङ्गुष्ठा स्वङ्गुलीतललक्षितौ।।5.10.17।। संहतौ परिघाकारौ वृत्तौ करिकरोपमौ। विक्षिप्तौ शयने शुभ्रे पञ्चशीर्षाविवोरगौ।।5.10.18।। शशक्षतजकल्पेन सुशीतेन सुगन्धिना। चन्दनेन परार्ध्येन स्वनुलिप्तौ स्वलङ्कृतौ।।5.10.19।। उत्तमस्त्रीविमृदितौ गन्धोत्तमनिषेवितौ। यक्षपन्नगगन्धर्वदेवदानवराविणौ।।5.10.20।।
348.e: Hanuman saw the great Ravana's arms, which were like a pair of Indra's flag staff adorned with golden straps. The arms bore the marks of wounds caused by Airavata, (Indra's elephant), torn by the thunderbolt of Indra in war, and wounded by the discus of Lord Visnu. His strong, fleshy, wellbuilt arms, having auspicious thumbnails, shapely fingers and palms, pressed together, resembled the iron crowbars or beam used for main doors. The arms resembled elephant's trunks, tossed on a clean bed, resembling two fivehooded snakes (fingers like hoods), besmeared with cool, fragrant, red sandalpaste of excellent quality which looked red like the hare's blood. They were well massaged  by the best of women with fine, fragrant sandal paste. They were the arms which could make yakshas, pannagas, gods and demons roar in fear at their sight.

348.sa: ददर्श स कपिस्तत्र बाहू शयनसंस्थितौ। मन्दरस्यांतरे सुप्तौ महाही रुषिताविव।।5.10.21।।
348.e: The vanara, gazed at the arms of Ravana placed on the couch that appeared like two angry snakes asleep in a cave on (the lap) of mount Mandara.

348.sa: ताभ्यां स परिपूर्णाभ्यां भुजाभ्यां राक्षसेश्वरः। शुशुभेऽचलसङ्काशः शृङ्गाभ्यामिव मन्दरः।।5.10.22।।
348.e: The lord of demons looked splendid like a mountain with his long, fully developed arms. He appeared like Mandara mountain with two lofty peaks.

348.sa: चूतपुन्नागसुरभिर्वकुलोत्तमसंयुतः। मृष्टान्नरससंयुक्तः पानगन्धपुरस्कृतः।।5.10.23।। तस्य राक्षससिंहस्य निश्चक्राम महामुखात्। शयानस्य विनिःश्वासः पूरयन्निव तद् गृहम्।।5.10.24।।
348.e: The breath released from the huge mouth of that lion of demons carried the fragrance of mango and punnaga as well as excellent Bakula flowers. It exuded the aroma of rich and delicious food and different drink. It was as though pervading the whole chamber.

348.sa: चूतपुन्नागसुरभिर्वकुलोत्तमसंयुतः। मृष्टान्नरससंयुक्तः पानगन्धपुरस्कृतः।।5.10.23।। तस्य राक्षससिंहस्य निश्चक्राम महामुखात्। शयानस्य विनिःश्वासः पूरयन्निव तद् गृहम्।।5.10.24।।
348.e: The breath released from the huge mouth of that lion of demons carried the fragrance of mango and punnaga as well as excellent Bakula flowers. It exuded the aroma of rich and delicious food and different drink. It was as though pervading the whole chamber.

348.sa: मुक्तामणिविचित्रेण काञ्चनेन विराजितम्। मकुटेनापवृत्तेन कुण्डलोज्वलिताननम्।।5.10.25।। रक्तचन्दनदिग्धेन तथा हारेण शोभिना। पीनायतविशालेन वक्षसाऽभिविराजितम्।।5.10.26।। पाण्डरेणापविद्धेन क्षौमेण क्षतजेक्षणम्। महार्हेण सुसंवीतं पीतेनोत्तमवाससा।।5.10.27।। माषराशिप्रतीकाशं निश्श्वसन्तं भुजङ्गवत्। गाङ्गे महति तोयान्ते प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्।।5.10.28।। चतुर्भिः काञ्चनैर्दीपैद्धीप्यमानचतुर्दिशम्। प्रकाशीकृतसर्वाङ्गं मेघं विद्युद्गणैरिव।।5.10.29।। पादमूलगताश्चापि ददर्श सुमहात्मनः। पत्नी: स प्रियभार्यस्य तस्य रक्षःपतेर्गृहे।।5.10.30।।
348.e: Hanuman saw Ravana, whose face was lit up by his earrings. His shining headgear studded with gold and pearls was set aside. His fleshy, broad chest on which the pearl necklace had slightly receded from its position(as he was asleep)  was shining along with the red sandal paste. He had put on a splendid white silken cloth which had also slipped a little and was covered with exquisitely  rich yellow upper garment. His eyes were bloodred. His body was comparable to a heap of blackbeans. He was sighing heavily like a hissing snake. He appeared like an elephant sleeping on the banks of the great river Ganges. With four golden lamps glowing on four sides of the bed,the four directions were illuminated. All his limbs lit up bright (with the glow of lamps), he looked like a cloud with streaks of lightning. His dear wives were seen resting at his feet in the palace of the lord of demons.

His fleshy, broad chest on which the pearl necklace had slightly receded from its position(as he was asleep)  was shining along with the red sandal paste. He had put on a splendid white silken cloth which had also slipped a little and was covered with exquisitely  rich yellow upper garment. His eyes were bloodred. His body was comparable to a heap of blackbeans. He was sighing heavily like a hissing snake. He appeared like an elephant sleeping on the banks of the great river Ganges. With four golden lamps glowing on four sides of the bed,the four directions were illuminated. All his limbs lit up bright (with the glow of lamps), he looked like a cloud with streaks of lightning. His dear wives were seen resting at his feet in the palace of the lord of demons.

348.sa: शशिप्रकाशवदनाश्चारुकुण्डलभूषिताः। अम्लानमाल्याभरणा ददर्श हरियूथपः।।5.10.31।।
348.e: Hanuman, the leader of vanaras found the wives of Ravana,  whose  faces were bright as the Moon, adorned with beautiful earrings and fresh floral garlands.

348.sa: नृत्तवादित्रकुशला राक्षसेन्द्रभुजाङ्कगाः। वराभरणधारिण्यो निषण्णा ददृशे हरिः।।5.10.32।।
348.e: Hanuman saw  the women there wearing fine jewellery, performing dances, playing musical instruments, and resting on the lap or leaning on the arms of the demon king.

348.sa: वज्रवैडूर्यगर्भाणि श्रवणान्तेषु योषिताम्। ददर्श तापनीयानि कुण्डलान्यङ्गदानि च।।5.10.33।।
348.e: He noticed on the earlobes of the the women gold earrings decked with diamonds and vaidurya. They were wearing shining armlets of gold.

348.sa: तासां चन्द्रोपमैर्वक्त्रैश्शुभैर्ललितकुण्डलैः। विरराज विमानं तन्नभस्तारागणैरिव।।5.10.34।।
348.e: There the beautiful moonlike faces of women Illumined by the lovely earrings lay on the cot which looked resplendent like the sky lit up with hosts of stars.

348.sa: मदव्यायामखिन्नास्ता राक्षसेन्द्रस्य योषितः। तेषु तेष्ववकाशेषु प्रसुप्तास्तनुमध्यमाः।।5.10.35।।
348.e: Exhausted by drinking and indulging in amorous sport, the consorts of Ravana slept here and there with their visible slender waists.

348.sa: अङ्गहारैस्तथैवान्या कोमलैर्नृत्तशालिनी। विन्यस्तशुभसर्वाङ्गी प्रसुप्ता वरवर्णिनी।।5.10.36।।
348.e: Another woman exceedingly beautiful and a delicate danseuse of beautiful complexion and rhythmic movements held her limbs in a dancing posture (though asleep) due to her habit .

348.sa: काचिद्वीणां परिष्वज्य प्रसुप्ता सम्प्रकाशते। महानदीप्रकीर्णेव नलिनी पोतमाश्रिता।।5.10.37।।
348.e: Another woman slept hugging her veena. She shone like a lotus plant flung in a large river, clinging on to a boat. (Veena is compared to a boat and the woman to a lotusplant in the ambience of flowing waters of the river. The entire hall had put up such a dynamic view showing hectic life of the inmates).

348.sa: अन्या कक्षगतेनैव मड्डुकेनासितेक्षणा। प्रसुप्ता भामिनी भाति बालपुत्रेव वत्सला।।5.10.38।।
348.e: A woman with dark eyes asleep with a drum placed in her armpit looked like a beautiful mother holding her loving baby (the drum was hung to her arm with a rope).

348.sa: पटहं चारुसर्वाङ्गी पीड्य शेते शुभस्तनी। चिरस्य रमणं लब्ध्वा परिष्वज्येव भामिनी।।5.10.39।।
348.e: Another charming beauty endowed with beautiful breasts lay hugging a tambourine as though a passionate woman lay embracing her lover whom she secured after a long time.

348.sa: काचिद्वंशं परिष्वज्य सुप्ता कमललोचना। रहः प्रियतमं गृह्य सकामेव च कामिनी।।5.10.40।।
348.e: Yet another lotuseyed lady slept embracing a lute as if a lovelorn woman lay clasping her lover.

348.sa: विपञ्चीं परिगृह्यान्या नियता नृत्तशालिनी। निद्रावशमनुप्राप्ता सह कान्तेव भामिनी।।5.10.41।।
348.e: Another selfpossessed lady, graceful in dance, holding a sevenstringed lute  was as though lying asleep with her beloved.

348.sa: अन्या कनकसङ्काशैर्मृदुपीनैर्मनोरमैः। मृदङ्गं परिपीड्याङ्गैः प्रसुप्ता मत्तलोचना।।5.10.42।।
348.e: Another lady with drunken eyes lay fast asleep holding a drum close to her beautiful bosom with her soft limbs. (These images show that these women were singing and dancing till late night and slept exhausted).

348.sa: भुजपार्श्वान्तरस्थेन कक्षगेन कृशोदरी। पणवेव सहानिन्द्या सुप्ता मदकृतश्रमा।।5.10.43।।
348.e: Another lady of slender belly, who had been exhausted by drunkeness was lying with a tabor pressed to her bosom and inserted in her armpit.

348.sa: डिण्डिमं परिगृह्यान्या तथैवासक्तडिण्डिमा। प्रसुप्ता तरुणं वत्समुपगूह्येव भामिनी।।5.10.44।।
348.e: One lovely woman and another held a drum and slept as if they were hugging their young child.

348.sa: काचिदाडम्बरं नारी भुजसंयोगपीडितम्। कृत्वा कमलपत्राक्षी प्रसुप्ता मदमोहिता।।5.10.45।।
348.e: Yet another with her eyes like lotus petals deluded with passion tightly held in her arms a musical instrument known as Adambaram and slept.

348.sa: कलशीमपविध्यान्या प्रसुप्ता भाति भामिनी। वसन्ते पुष्पशबला मालेव परिमार्जिता।।5.10.46।।
348.e: Another lovely lady was fast asleep, having turned a goblet of water  aside, yet another lay like a garland of variegated flowers in spring season.

348.sa: पाणिभ्यां च कुचौ काचित्सुवर्णकलशोपमौ। उपगूह्याबला सुप्ता निद्राबलपराजिता।।5.10.47।।
348.e: Overcome with sleep another woman lay pressing with her own hands her golden gobletlike breasts.

348.sa: अन्या कमलपत्राक्षी पूर्णेन्दुसदृशानना। अन्यामालिङ्ग्य सुश्रोणीं प्रसुप्ता मदविह्वला।।5.10.48।।
348.e: One woman with eyes like lotus petals and face like the fullmoon embraced another young woman of beautiful hips  and slept tipsy with drink.

348.sa: आतोद्यानि विचित्राणि परिष्वज्य वरस्त्रियः। निपीड्य च कुचैस्सुप्ता कामिन्यः कामुकानिव।।5.10.49।।
348.e: Some charming maidens held wonderful musical instruments pressing against their bosom and slept like passionate women embracing their loved ones.

348.sa: तासामेकान्तविन्यस्ते शयानां शयने शुभे। ददर्श रूपसम्पन्नामपरां स कपिः स्त्रियम्।।5.10.50।।
348.e: Hanuman saw some maidens lying on separate excellent beds, women richly  endowed with beautysleeping.

348.sa: मुक्तामणिसमायुक्तैर्भूषणैः सुविभूषिताम्। विभूषयन्तीमिव तत्स्वश्रिया भवनोत्तमम्।।5.10.51।। गौरीं कनकवर्णाभामिष्टामन्तः पुरेश्वरीम्। कपिर्मन्दोदरीं तत्र शयानां चारुरूपिणीम्।।5.10.52।।
348.e: Then the vanara saw  a very beautiful woman of golden complexion decked with pearls and gems and with ornaments as if illuminating the excellent mansion with her splendour She was the king's favourite and the chief queen, Mandodari.

348.sa: मुक्तामणिसमायुक्तैर्भूषणैः सुविभूषिताम्। विभूषयन्तीमिव तत्स्वश्रिया भवनोत्तमम्।।5.10.51।। गौरीं कनकवर्णाभामिष्टामन्तः पुरेश्वरीम्। कपिर्मन्दोदरीं तत्र शयानां चारुरूपिणीम्।।5.10.52।।
348.e: Then the vanara saw  a very beautiful woman of golden complexion decked with pearls and gems and with ornaments as if illuminating the excellent mansion with her splendour She was the king's favourite and the chief queen, Mandodari.

348.sa: स तां दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्भूषितां मारुतात्मजः। तर्कयामास सीतेति रूपयौवनसम्पदा।।5.10.53। हर्षेण महता युक्तो ननन्द हरियूथपः।
348.e: On seeing her embellished with ornaments, beauty and charm, the long armed son of the Windgod, the chief of the vanaras thought her to be Sita and rejoiced.

348.sa: आस्फोटयामास चुचुम्ब पुच्छं ननन्द चिक्रीड जगौ जगाम। स्तम्भानरोहन्निपपात भूमौ निदर्शयन् स्वां प्रकृतिं कपीनाम्।।5.10.54।।
348.e: He rejoiced clapping his palms, kissing his tail and jumping up, climbing up the pillars and jumping down on the ground in joy. Thus he exhibited his monkey nature. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे दशमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the tenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

349.sa: अवधूय च तां बुद्धिं बभूवावस्थितस्तदा। जगाम चापरां चिन्तां सीतां प्रति महाकपिः।।5.11.1।।
349.e: The great vanara, having rejected his judgement, started thinking again.

349.sa: न रामेण वियुक्ता सा स्वप्तुमर्हति भामिनी। न भोक्तुं वाप्यलङ्कर्तुं न पानमुपसेवितुम्।।5.11.2।। नान्यं नरमुपस्थातुं सुराणामपि चेश्वरम्। न हि रामसमः कश्चिद्विद्यते त्रिदशेष्वपि।।5.11.3।। अन्येयमिति निश्चित्य पानभूमौ चचार सः।
349.e: 'Lovely Sita, being away from Rama, will not sleep, will not eat or drink or adorn herself. How can she approach any other man even if he is the king of gods for there is none equal to Rama even among gods'. Having thus decided, Hanuman strolled about the banquet hall.

349.sa: न रामेण वियुक्ता सा स्वप्तुमर्हति भामिनी। न भोक्तुं वाप्यलङ्कर्तुं न पानमुपसेवितुम्।।5.11.2।। नान्यं नरमुपस्थातुं सुराणामपि चेश्वरम्। न हि रामसमः कश्चिद्विद्यते त्रिदशेष्वपि।।5.11.3।। अन्येयमिति निश्चित्य पानभूमौ चचार सः।
349.e: 'Lovely Sita, being away from Rama, will not sleep, will not eat or drink or adorn herself. How can she approach any other man even if he is the king of gods for there is none equal to Rama even among gods'. Having thus decided, Hanuman strolled about the banquet hall.

349.sa: क्रीडितेनापराः क्लान्ता गीतेन च तथाऽपराः।।5.11.4।। नृत्तेन चापराः क्लान्ताः पानविप्रहतास्तथा।
349.e: Some women were fatigued after sporting, similarly some were exhausted after singing. Others were tired through dancing and some were worn out by continuous drinking.

349.sa: मुरजेषु मृदङ्गेषु पीठिकासु च संस्थिताः।।5.11.5।। तथाऽऽस्तरणमुख्येषु संविष्टाश्चापराः स्त्रियः।
349.e: Some women reclined on tabors, some on murajas, and some on drums and hassocks while some slept on excellent couches.

349.sa: अङ्गनानां सहस्रेण भूषितेन विभूषणैः।।5.11.6।। रूपसल्लापशीलेन युक्तगीतार्थभाषिणा। देशकालाभियुक्तेन युक्तवाक्याभिधायिना।।5.11.7।। रताभिरतसंसुप्तं ददर्श हरियूथपः।
349.e: The monkey leader saw thousands of  beautiful women asleep after long dalliance. Some of them were adorned with ornaments, some were good at arguments and versed in the appreciation of songs, some were aware of the appropriate time and place and some were adept in right expressions.

349.sa: अङ्गनानां सहस्रेण भूषितेन विभूषणैः।।5.11.6।। रूपसल्लापशीलेन युक्तगीतार्थभाषिणा। देशकालाभियुक्तेन युक्तवाक्याभिधायिना।।5.11.7।। रताभिरतसंसुप्तं ददर्श हरियूथपः।
349.e: The monkey leader saw thousands of  beautiful women asleep after long dalliance. Some of them were adorned with ornaments, some were good at arguments and versed in the appreciation of songs, some were aware of the appropriate time and place and some were adept in right expressions.

349.sa: तासां मध्ये महाबाहुः शुशुभे राक्षसेश्वरः।।5.11.8।। गोष्ठे महति मुख्यानां गवां मध्ये यथा वृषः।
349.e: In the midst of these women the longarmed lord of demons shone like a (majestic) bull in a big cowshed.

349.sa: स राक्षसेन्द्रः शुशुभे ताभिः परिवृतस्स्वयम्।।5.11.9।। करेणुभिर्यथाऽरण्ये परिकीर्णो महाद्विपः।
349.e: Surrounded by the women, the demon king shone like a proud elephant attended by many female elephants scattered in a dense forest.

349.sa: सर्वकामैरुपेतां च पानभूमिं महात्मनः।।5.11.10।। ददर्श हरिशार्दूलस्तस्य रक्षःपतेर्गृहे।
349.e: The tiger among vanaras saw at the great Ravana's palace a drinking place where everything one desires was provided.

349.sa: मृगाणां महिषाणां च वराहाणां च भागशः।।5.11.11।। तत्र न्यस्तानि मांसानि पानभूमौ ददर्श सः।
349.e: There at the drinking hall the meat of deer, buffaloes and boars portioned and placed.

349.sa: रौक्मेषु च विशालेषु भाजनेष्वर्धभक्षितान्।।5.11.12।। ददर्श हरिशार्दूलो मयूरान् कुक्कुटांस्तथा।
349.e: The tiger among vanaras also saw there meat of peacocks and chicken placed in large golden vessels, some half eaten.

349.sa: वराहवार्ध्राणसकान् दधिसौवर्चलायुतान्।।5.11.13।। शल्यान् मृगमयूरांश्च हनुमानन्ववैक्षत।
349.e: Hanuman saw the meat of pigs and jungle fowls, deer, peacocks and bones marinated with yoghurt and special kinds of salt.

349.sa: क्रकरान्विविधान् सिद्धांश्चकोरानर्धभक्षितान्।।5.11.14।। महिषानेकशल्यांश्च छागांश्च कृतनिष्ठितान्। लेह्यानुच्चावचान्पेयान् भोज्यानि विविधानि च।।5.11.15।।
349.e: He saw several kinds of (nonvegetarian) food like cooked meat of fowls, ruddy geese, buffaloes, goats, fishes as well as food for licking. (Food is of four kinds  1) भक्ष्य which can be chewed 2) भोज्य ordinary solid, semisolid food which can be consumed  3) लेह्य food for licking  4) चोष्य liquid food (which can be sipped)).

349.sa: क्रकरान्विविधान् सिद्धांश्चकोरानर्धभक्षितान्।।5.11.14।। महिषानेकशल्यांश्च छागांश्च कृतनिष्ठितान्। लेह्यानुच्चावचान्पेयान् भोज्यानि विविधानि च।।5.11.15।।
349.e: He saw several kinds of (nonvegetarian) food like cooked meat of fowls, ruddy geese, buffaloes, goats, fishes as well as food for licking. (Food is of four kinds  1) भक्ष्य which can be chewed 2) भोज्य ordinary solid, semisolid food which can be consumed  3) लेह्य food for licking  4) चोष्य liquid food (which can be sipped)).

349.sa: तथाऽऽम्ललवणोत्तंसैर्विविधैरागषाडबैः। हारनूपुरकेयूरैरपविद्धैर्महाधनैः।।5.11.16।। पानभाजनविक्षिप्तैः फलैश्च विविधैरपि। कृतपुष्पोपहारा भूरधिकं पुष्यति श्रियम्।।5.11.17।।
349.e: The banquet hall looked splendid with food seasoned with salt and sour ingredients. There was ragashadavas (syrup made with grapes, pomegranates, different juices like half ripe mangoes and seasoned with ginger cardomom, butter etc). Heavy chains, anklets and shouldersstraps were thrown aside. (The people relaxed while eating and drinking and discarded heavy ornaments). Many glasses were found scattered or drinks spilt on the floor after use.Many fruits and flowers were kept.

349.sa: तथाऽऽम्ललवणोत्तंसैर्विविधैरागषाडबैः। हारनूपुरकेयूरैरपविद्धैर्महाधनैः।।5.11.16।। पानभाजनविक्षिप्तैः फलैश्च विविधैरपि। कृतपुष्पोपहारा भूरधिकं पुष्यति श्रियम्।।5.11.17।।
349.e: The banquet hall looked splendid with food seasoned with salt and sour ingredients. There was ragashadavas (syrup made with grapes, pomegranates, different juices like half ripe mangoes and seasoned with ginger cardomom, butter etc). Heavy chains, anklets and shouldersstraps were thrown aside. (The people relaxed while eating and drinking and discarded heavy ornaments). Many glasses were found scattered or drinks spilt on the floor after use.Many fruits and flowers were kept.

349.sa: तत्र तत्र च विन्यस्तै: सुश्लिष्टैश्शयनासनैः। पानभूमिर्विना वह्निं प्रदीप्तेवोपलक्ष्यते।।5.11.18।।
349.e: Good couches and different kinds of seats were wellarranged in the banquet hall. The place appeared as if it was glowing witout fire.

349.sa: बहुप्रकारैर्विविधैर्वरसंस्कारसंस्कृतैः। मांसैः कुशलसम्पृक्तैः पानभूमिगतैः पृथक्।।5.11.19।।
349.e: In the banquet hall there were many types of meat arranged in a number of ways. They were cooked by experts by seasoning them with choicest ingredients.

349.sa: दिव्याः प्रसन्ना विविधाः सुराः कृतसुरा अपि। शर्कराऽसवमाध्वीकपुष्पासवफलासवाः।।5.11.20।। वासचूर्णैश्च विविधैर्मृष्टास्तैस्तैः पृथक् पृथक्।
349.e: There were many types of wonderful and pleasing wine extracted from sugarcane, honey , fruits and flowers. They were good even though fermented and made delicious by seasoning with aromatic spices.

349.sa: सन्तता शुशुभे भूमिर्माल्यैश्च बहुसंस्थितैः।।5.11.21।। हिरण्मयैश्च विविधैर्भाजनैः स्फाटिकैरपि। जाम्बूनदमयैश्चान्यैः करकैरभिसंवृता।।5.11.22।।
349.e: (The banquet hall) appeared beautiful with many kinds of garlands arranged in different locations. Also there were vessels made of pure gold, crystalware and jars spread all over.

349.sa: सन्तता शुशुभे भूमिर्माल्यैश्च बहुसंस्थितैः।।5.11.21।। हिरण्मयैश्च विविधैर्भाजनैः स्फाटिकैरपि। जाम्बूनदमयैश्चान्यैः करकैरभिसंवृता।।5.11.22।।
349.e: (The banquet hall) appeared beautiful with many kinds of garlands arranged in different locations. Also there were vessels made of pure gold, crystalware and jars spread all over.

349.sa: राजतेषु च कुम्भेषु जाम्बूनदमयेषु च। पानश्रेष्ठं तदा भूरि कपिस्तत्र ददर्श ह।।5.11.23।।
349.e: Hanuman saw the best of wines in large quantities kept in silver and pure gold pots.

349.sa: ﻿सोऽपश्यच्छातकुम्भानि सीधोर्मणिमयानि च। राजतानि च पूर्णानि भाजनानि महाकपिः।।5.11.24।।
349.e: ﻿ The great monkey saw the wine jars made of gold and silver studded with crystals and gems.

349.sa: क्वचिदल्पावशेषाणि क्वचित्पीतानि सर्वशः। क्वचिन्नैव प्रपीतानि पानानि स ददर्श ह।।5.11.25।।
349.e: He saw wine jars at one place, some fully drained, and at another place not touched at all.

349.sa: क्वचिद् भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान् क्वचित्पानानि भागशः। क्वचिदन्नावशेषाणि पश्यन्वै विचचार ह।।5.11.26।।
349.e: He moved about looking at different types of eatables and drinks arranged separately along with the left over food.

349.sa: क्वचित्प्रभिन्नैः करकैः क्वचिदालोलितैर्घटैः। क्वचित्संपृक्तमाल्यानि जलानि च फलानि च।।5.11.27।।
349.e: At some places he saw broken pots, at other places rolling pots and elsewhere flower garlands strewn and mixed up with water and fruits.

349.sa: शयनान्यत्र नारीणां शुभ्राणि बहुधा पुनः। परस्परं समाश्लिष्य काश्चित्सुप्ता वराङ्गनाः।।5.11.28।।
349.e: Hanuman saw many beds some unused and some occupied by lovely women sleeping, embracing one another.

349.sa: काश्चिच्च वस्त्रमन्यस्यास्स्वपन्त्याः परिधाय च। आहृत्य चाबलाः सुप्ता निद्राबलपराजिताः।।5.11.29।।
349.e: Overcome with sleep some women pulled clothes of other women and covered their bodies with them.

349.sa: तासामुच्छवासवातेन वस्त्रं माल्यं च गात्रजम्। नात्यर्थं स्पन्दते चित्रं प्राप्य मन्दमिवानिलम्।।5.11.30।।
349.e: The lovely clothes and garlands on the bodies of women were moving mildly by their exhalations as if shaken by the gentle breeze.

349.sa: चन्दनस्य च शीतस्य शीधोर्मधुरसस्य च। विविधस्य च माल्यस्य धूपस्य विविधस्य च।।5.11.31।। बहुधा मारुतस्तत्र गन्धं विविधमुद्वहन्।
349.e: With the many scents of cool sandal, of sweetsmelling wines of diverse kinds, as well as flower garlands of several types and of incense burning in that hall, the cool wind blew spreading several fragrances all over.

349.sa: स्नानानां चन्दनानां च धूपानां चैव मूर्छितः।।5.11.32।। प्रववौ सुरभिर्गन्धो विमाने पुष्पके तदा।
349.e: The wind wafting through the Pushpaka chariot carried the fragrance of the cool sandalpaste used in bath and the sweet smell of wines and thick smoke of fragrance spread further.

349.sa: श्यामावदातास्तत्रान्याः काश्चित्कृष्णा वराङ्गनाः।।5.11.33।। काश्चित् काञ्चनवर्णाङ्ग्यः प्रमदा राक्षसालये।
349.e: There in the demons abode were women who were fair, some lovely with dark and others with golden complexion.

349.sa: तासां निद्रावशत्वाच्च मदनेन विमूर्छितम्।।5.11.34।। पद्मिनीनां प्रसुप्तानां रूपमासीद्यथैव हि।
349.e: Withered due to indulgence in sex they were overcome with sleep. The charm of the women was like the lotus creepers with closed lotuses .

349.sa: एवं सर्वमशेषेण रावणान्तः पुरं कपिः।।5.11.35।। ददर्श सुमहातेजाः न ददर्श च जानकीम्।
349.e: Brilliant Hanuman ransacked the harem of Ravana but found no Janaki.

349.sa: निरीक्षमाणश्च तदा ताः स्त्रियः स महाकपिः।।5.11.36।। जगाम महतीं चिन्तां धर्मसाध्वसशङ्कितः।
349.e: The great monkey was very much worried as he thought he had transgressed the moral code by watching the women.

349.sa: परदारावरोधस्य प्रसुप्तस्य निरीक्षणम्।।5.11.37।। इदं खलु ममात्यर्थं धर्मलोपं करिष्यति।
349.e: 'Observing the wives of others in this manner in their inner chambers very much amounts to transgression of moral code  by me'. ( thought he)

349.sa: न हि मे परदाराणां दृष्टिर्विषयवर्तिनी।।5.11.38।। अयं चात्र मया दृष्टः परदारापरिग्रहः।
349.e: 'I did see these wives of another, but not with a sensual mind. I have only seen them but not with foul intention'.

349.sa: तस्य प्रादुरभूच्चिन्ता पुनरन्या मनस्विनः।।5.11.39।। निश्चितैकान्तचित्तस्य कार्यनिश्चयदर्शिनी।
349.e: Another  bright idea struck the highly sensible Hanuman, who had a clear vision of the task ahead-- 'I was firm and singleminded in my direction regarding the task ahead' (thought he).

349.sa: कामं दृष्टा मया सर्वा विश्वस्ता रावणस्त्रियः।।5.11.40।। न हि मे मनसः किञ्चिद्वैकृत्यमुपजायते।
349.e: 'It is true I saw all the loyal wives of Ravana but without any foul desire. Indeed in my mind no passionate feeling was ever aroused'.

349.sa: मनो हि हेतुः सर्वेषामिन्द्रियाणां प्रवर्तने।।5.11.41।। शुभाशुभास्ववस्थासु तच्च मे सुव्यवस्थितम्।
349.e: 'Mind propels the sense organs to do good or bad deeds. (But) my mind is firmly esatablished in righteousness'.

349.sa: नान्यत्र हि मया शक्या वैदेही परिमार्गितुम्।।5.11.42।। स्त्रियो हि स्त्रीषु दृश्यन्ते सदा सम्परिमार्गणे।
349.e: 'It is not possible for me to look for Vaidehi elsewhere. During such search operations one always looks for women among women.'

349.sa: यस्य सत्त्वस्य या योनिस्तस्यां तत्परिमार्ग्यते। न शक्या प्रमदा नष्टा मृगीषु परिमार्गितुम्।।5.11.43।।
349.e: 'One has to search a creature among its own species. It is not possible to find a lost woman in the herd of female deer'.

349.sa: तदिदं मार्गितं तावच्छुद्धेन मनसा मया।।5.11.44।। रावणान्तःपुरं सर्वं दृश्यते न तु जानकी।
349.e: 'I searched all over Ravana's harem with a pure mind but I have not seen Janaki'.

349.sa: देवगन्धर्वकन्याश्च नागकन्याश्च वीर्यवान्।।5.11.45।। अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान्नैवापश्यत जानकीम्।
349.e: Even while valiant Hanuman was looking among the daughters of gods, gandharvas and nagas he could not find Janaki.

349.sa: तामपश्यन्कपिस्तत्र पश्यञ्श्चान्या परस्त्रियः।।5.11.46।। अपक्रम्य तदा वीरः प्रध्यातुमुपचक्रमे।
349.e: Heroic Hanuman, unable to find Sita among the women, moved aside and started thinking.

349.sa: स भूयस्तु परं श्रीमान् मारुतिर्यत्नमास्थितः।।5.11.47।। आपानभूमिमुत्सृज्य तद्विचेतुं प्रचक्रमे।
349.e: Illustrious Hanuman left the banquet hall to renew his effort in search of Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकादशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eleventh sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

350.sa: स तस्य मध्ये भवनस्य मारुति र्लतागृहांश्चित्रगृहान्निशागृहान्। जगाम सीतां प्रति दर्शनोत्सुको न चैव तां पश्यति चारुदर्शनाम्।।5.12.1।।
350.e: Anxious to find Sita, Hanuman revisited the bowers of creepers, picture galleries and domitories located in the midst of the mansion, but  did not find that beautiful Sita.

350.sa: स चिन्तयामास ततो महाकपिः प्रियामपश्यन्रघुनन्दनस्य ताम्। ध्रुवं हि सीता म्रियते यथा न मे विचिन्वतो दर्शनमेति मैथिली।।5.12.2।।
350.e: The great monkey, unable to find the beloved of Rama thought Sita might not be surviving. So he started thinking, ' I could not see her even though I have searched all over'.

350.sa: सा राक्षसानां प्रवरेण जानकी स्वशीलसंरक्ष्णतत्परा सती। अनेन नूनं प्रति दुष्टकर्मणा हता भवेदार्यपथे परे स्थिता।।5.12.3।।
350.e: 'Janaki, follower of noble path, anxious to protect her chastity must have been killed by the wicked demon king.

350.sa: विरूपरूपा विकृता विवर्चसो महानना दीर्घविरूपदर्शनाः। समीक्ष्य सा राक्षसराजयोषितो भयाद्विनष्टा जनकेश्वरात्मजा।।5.12.4।।
350.e: 'The daughter of Janaka might have collapsed out of fear, looking at the distorted faces of ugly, tall and monstrous demon maids of Ravana.

350.sa: सीतामदृष्ट्वा ह्यनवाप्य पौरुषं विहृत्य कालं सह वानरैश्चिरम्। न मेऽस्ति सुग्रीवसमीपगा गतिः सुतीक्ष्णदण्डो बलवांश्च वानरः।।5.12.5।।
350.e: 'I have spent a long time with vanaras. I have not  succeded in my efforts to find Sita. I dare not see Sugriva now without finding Sita and without fulfilling my task. Sugriva will punish me severely. There is no way out.'

350.sa: दृष्टमन्तःपुरं सर्वं दृष्टा रावणयोषितः। न सीता दृश्यते साध्वीवृथा जातो मम श्रमः।।5.12.6।।
350.e: 'I have searched all over the harem. Ravana's women have been seen. (Yet) I have not been able to see noble Sita. My efforts have been wasted'.

350.sa: किं नु मां वानराः सर्वे गतं वक्ष्यन्ति सङ्गताः। गत्वा तत्र त्वया वीर किं कृतं तद्वदस्व नः।।5.12.7।।
350.e: 'What will the vanaras say when I return? What should I speak when they ask me: O hero, what did you accomplish there?'

350.sa: अदृष्ट्वा किं प्रवक्ष्यामि तामहं जनकात्मजाम्। ध्रुवं प्रायमुपैष्यन्ति कालस्य व्यतिवर्तने।।5.12.8।।
350.e: 'Since the time limit has exceeded and Janaki is not spotted, surely the vanaras would sit and wait unto death. What am I going to say'?

350.sa: किं वा वक्ष्यति वृद्धश्च जाम्बवानाङ्गदश्च सः। गतं पारं समुद्रस्य वानराश्च समागताः।।5.12.9।।
350.e: 'What will the elderly Jambavan say? What will young prince Angada and other vanaras collected there say when I reach the seashore to meet them'.

350.sa: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। अनिर्वेदो हि सततं सर्वार्थेषु प्रवर्तकः।।5.12.10।।
350.e: Wise Hanuman once again declared, 'being free from despair is the root cause of prosperity. Freedom from despondency gives supreme happiness and leads to success'.

350.sa: करोति सफलं जन्तोः कर्म यत्तत्करोति सः। तस्मादनिर्वेदकृतं यत्नं चेष्टेऽहमुत्तमम्।।5.12.11।। भूयस्तावद्विचेष्यामि देशान्रावणपालितान्।
350.e: 'The action of a living being certainly bears fruit. Therefore, I shall put forth my best effort without feeling despondent. I will once again search everywhere in Lanka ruled  by Ravana'.

350.sa: आपानशाला विचितास्तथा पुष्पगृहाणि च।।5.12.12।। चित्रशालाश्च विचिता भूयः क्रीडागृहाणि च। निष्कुटान्तररथ्याश्च विमानानि च सर्वशः।।5.12.13।।
350.e: 'I have searched the banquet halls, bowers of creepers, picture galleries and gymnasiums. I have searched everywhere through the paths of gardens and mansions, harems and the Pushpaka chariot also.

350.sa: आपानशाला विचितास्तथा पुष्पगृहाणि च।।5.12.12।। चित्रशालाश्च विचिता भूयः क्रीडागृहाणि च। निष्कुटान्तररथ्याश्च विमानानि च सर्वशः।।5.12.13।।
350.e: 'I have searched the banquet halls, bowers of creepers, picture galleries and gymnasiums. I have searched everywhere through the paths of gardens and mansions, harems and the Pushpaka chariot also.

350.sa: इति सञ्चिन्त्य भूयोऽपि विचेतुमुपचक्रमे। भूमीगृहांश्चैत्यगृहान् गृहातिगृहकानपि।।5.12.14।।
350.e: Thinking thus, he started searching once again the basement cells, temples, homes within homes.

350.sa: उत्पतन्निष्पतंश्चापि तिष्ठन्गच्छन् पुनः पुनः। अपावृण्वंश्च द्वाराणि कवाटान्यवघाटयन्।।5.12.15।। प्रविशन्निष्पतंश्चापि प्रपतन्नुत्पतन्नपि। सर्वमप्यवकाशं स विचचार महाकपिः।।5.12.16।।
350.e: The great vanara searched all over again and again jumping up and down, stopping for a while and moving, opening and closing doors, by crossing, entering and exiting, jumping up and down. Thus he moved about and searched whereever there was scope to search

350.sa: उत्पतन्निष्पतंश्चापि तिष्ठन्गच्छन् पुनः पुनः। अपावृण्वंश्च द्वाराणि कवाटान्यवघाटयन्।।5.12.15।। प्रविशन्निष्पतंश्चापि प्रपतन्नुत्पतन्नपि। सर्वमप्यवकाशं स विचचार महाकपिः।।5.12.16।।
350.e: The great vanara searched all over again and again jumping up and down, stopping for a while and moving, opening and closing doors, by crossing, entering and exiting, jumping up and down. Thus he moved about and searched whereever there was scope to search

350.sa: चतुरङ्गुलमात्रोऽपि नावकाशः स विद्यते। रावणान्तःपुरे तस्मिन् यं कपिर्न जगाम सः।।5.12.17।।
350.e: Even a space of four fingers in the inner chambers of Ravana was not left out in his search for Sita.

350.sa: प्राकारान्तररथ्याश्च वेदिकाश्चैत्यसंश्रयाः। दीर्घिकाः पुष्करिण्यश्च सर्वं तेनावलोकितम्।।5.12.18।।
350.e: He moved in the lanes inside the boundary walls, around the shrines, altars, wells and tanks whereever it was possible to look for.

350.sa: राक्षस्यो विविधाकारा विरूपा विकृतास्तथा। दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न तु सा जनकात्मजा।।5.12.19।।
350.e: Hanuman could see only ogresses of different typesugly, deformed but could not find the daughter of Janaka.

350.sa: रूपेणाप्रतिमा लोके वरा विद्याधरस्त्रियः। दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न तु राघवनन्दिनी।।5.12.20।।
350.e: Hanuman could see even the women of vidyadharas who were matchless in beauty among women in the world but not Janaki the beloved of Raghava.

350.sa: नागकन्या वरारोहाः पूर्णचन्र्दनिभाननाः। दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न तु सीता सुमध्यमा।।5.12.21।।
350.e: Hanuman could see there moonfaced daughters of nagas with charming limbs but not the slimwaisted Sita.

350.sa: प्रमथ्य राक्षसेन्द्रेण नागकन्या बलाद्धृताः। दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न सा जनकनन्दिनी।।5.12.22।।
350.e: Hanuman saw the daghters of nagas kidnapped by Ravana forcibly after victory in war but not Sita, the delight of Janaka.

350.sa: सोऽपश्यंस्तां महाबाहुः पश्यंश्चान्या वरस्त्रियः। विषसाद मुहुर्धीमान् हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।।5.12.23।।
350.e: The longarmed Hanuman, son of the Windgod was able to see other great women but not Sita. So he became despondent.

350.sa: उद्योगं वानरेन्द्राणां प्लवनं सागरस्य च। व्यर्थं वीक्ष्यानिलसुतश्चिन्तां पुनरुपागमत्।।5.12.24।।
350.e: The son of the Wind god, the great monkey realised the futility of his efforts in crossing the sea. He brooded again.

350.sa: अवतीर्य विमानाच्च हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। चिन्तामुपजगामाथ शोकोपहतचेतनः।।5.12.25।।
350.e: Hanuman, son of the Windgod, came out of the aerial chariot, mind stricken with grief and started thinking again. इत्यार्षे  श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे द्वादशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the twelfth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
